items.title: AuxoAI, which helps large businesses build and deploy AI systems, raised a $20.7M Series A led by NTTVC to accelerate growth and scale (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
items.title_en: AuxoAI, which helps large businesses build and deploy AI systems, raised a $20.7M Series A led by NTTVC to accelerate growth and scale (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
items.author: SiliconANGLE
items.article_content:
SHARE


	
	
		
			
				
					
						UPDATED 09:00 EDT / OCTOBER 20 2026

AuxoAI Inc., an enterprise engineering and consulting company that helps large businesses build and deploy artificial intelligence systems, today announced it has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding to accelerate growth and scale its enterprise AI consulting model.

The company said it has spent over three years working with Global 2000 enterprises and strategic partners, bringing AI into the core of their operations.  It focuses on combining business-process expertise, data engineering and AI agents – autonomous systems that use artificial intelligence to work with little or no human oversight, with deep insight into company data to complete long-term tasks.

AuxoAI builds AI solutions by sending on-site engineers and strategy teams to understand enterprise culture, data, workflow automation and customer engagement to tailor experiences to business and employee needs.

At the core of the company’s platform is Damia, which the company describes as an FDE Workbench, or “forward-deployed engineer” toolkit that also transforms data into applications and licenses for customers. It combines reusable agent capacities with tools for capturing a company’s business knowledge and processes.

The company said that over the years, it has learned how to work with customers to encode relevant knowledge and relationships and use that to create AI agents around the company’s processes. This preserves what the team learns in software and structured knowledge, rather than only interviews or paper documents, but in living software that can work alongside employees.

The company calls this effect “intelligence embedded in the work itself,” where consulting treats AI as a lever or tool for the customer rather than an end product.

AuxoAI partners with companies that businesses already know and trust, including Google LLC, Amazon Web Services Inc., Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc. and Microsoft Corp., allowing the company to provide enterprise-ready AI, cloud, data and productivity via these platforms.

NTT Venture Capital, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT Inc., led the funding round. The round also included participation from prominent industry executives and strategic investors, such as George Still Jr., partner emeritus at Norwest Venture Partners; Amit Zavery, president, chief product officer and chief operating officer at ServiceNow Inc.; and Giacomo Sonnino, managing director at Charlesbank Capital Partners and former chief operating officer of Quantum Black North America.

NTTVC’s portfolio includes Anthropic PBC, which will bring on another major artificial intelligence leader to extend AuxoAI’s capabilities.

The company said the new funding will serve to accelerate the next phase of its journey to expand its global reach. It aims to provide onsite consulting talent for enterprise AI transformation, invest in proprietary technology and AI-native delivery capabilities, and scale up its presence and strategic ecosystem.

Founded by tech visionaries John Furrier and Dave Vellante, SiliconANGLE Media has built a dynamic ecosystem of industry-leading digital media brands that reach 15+ million elite tech professionals. Our new proprietary theCUBE AI Video Cloud is breaking ground in audience interaction, leveraging theCUBEai.com neural network to help technology companies make data-driven decisions and stay at the forefront of industry conversations.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
items.title_en: Mark Zuckerberg Agrees to Stay in California Despite Billionaires’ Tax Ballot Measure
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
During a dinner with Meta board members on September 9, Zuckerberg informed them that he was considering leaving California because of the measure, known as Proposition 40, and that he planned to list his Palo Alto, California home for sale four days later, the 109-page filing stated. The ballot proposal, which could be subject to lawsuits even if voters approve it, calls for a one-time 5 percent tax on stock and other assets held by billionaires in the state as of January 2026.

Many wealthy individuals, including Zuckerberg, currently avoid significant tax payments by borrowing against their shares and taking low salaries—$1 annually in the Meta CEO’s case. Zuckerberg purchased a home in Florida this past February, the Wall Street Journal reported at the time.

His potential cross-country move concerned a special committee of the board, whose members included attorney Robert Kimmitt, venture capitalist Charlie Songhurst, and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu. “The special committee was mindful about the difficulties the company faced during the COVID-19 pandemic when Zuckerberg could not be physically present with the company’s management team and did not want the company to face similar challenges going forward,” according to Wednesday’s filing.

Within days of the Meta board dinner, the special committee and Zuckerberg reached an agreement that links his ability to sell special company shares to his continued residence in California. It was finalized a week ago, and on Wednesday, Meta announced the details. It plans to create a new class of shares that hold no voting power. Selling these shares could potentially help raise funds for Meta’s expensive investments into AI data centers, without diluting Zuckerberg’s existing voting control.

All existing shareholders will receive the new nonvoting shares automatically in proportion to their existing holdings. Under what Meta called a “Founder Alignment Agreement” with Zuckerberg, he can sell 20 percent of those new shares to help pay any taxes he may owe. The remaining 80 percent would be available for sale in chunks over the next eight years as long as he remains in California. Any attempt to sell them early would require offloading some of his voting shares “unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere.”

Notably, the agreement specifies that Zuckerberg merely has to remain wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, so it’s possible that both he and the company could move together to another state. A number of California companies left for Texas, Nevada, and other states in recent years. Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page are among the handful of billionaires widely believed to have exited California over the potential tax.

But with much of the most pioneering AI development happening in Silicon Valley, leaving the city of Menlo Park could be a difficult proposition for the Meta board to stomach. “The goal is to keep Zuckerberg continuing to lead the company from California and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs,” the filing stated, referring to the company unit behind its recent Muse AI models.

In the end, the exercise may have been for naught. Recent polling in California suggests that with about $129 million spent campaigning against Prop 40, it will fail to muster enough votes.

items.title: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
items.title_en: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
items.author: The Hacker News
items.article_content:
GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014.

The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an instance updated then is in range again.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, is rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale, the maximum. GitLab says that, under certain conditions, it could allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the server due to an integer overflow during the compilation of a specially crafted regular expression.

GitLab has not said what those conditions are. The company reports no sign the flaw has been used in attacks, and it is not listed in the U.S. CISA catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities as of October 22.

Only self-managed installations need to act. GitLab.com already runs the fixed version, and GitLab Dedicated tenants on the internal releases 19.3.5-internal0 and 19.4.2-internal0 or later already have the fix.

The table below pairs each release branch with the version that fixes it.

Four of those versions are older than GitLab normally patches. The company's policy covers the current release and the previous two monthly releases, which, as of today, are 19.5, 19.4, and 19.3.

GitLab said it backported this fix to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, and 19.2.9 on top of its standard releases, a step it reserves for severe issues.

The reason the flaw reaches so far back is the part of GitLab that failed. The regular-expression compiler is Ruby's built-in engine, called Onigmo, which GitLab ships inside its own packages and patches in its own builds. A weakness in that engine is present wherever GitLab has shipped it, which is every release since 7.0.

GitLab also published two detection rules to help self-managed administrators look for exploitation attempts, named "Onigmo native worker crash" and "Org mode render error burst." They are part of the company's open-source TLDR framework, which writes each detection in the Sigma format against GitLab's own application logs.

GitLab has not said what preconditions an attacker needs to reach the compiler, so administrators cannot yet rule themselves out by configuration; the fix is the only certain protection, and GitLab's advisory offers no interim workaround.

This is the fourth code-execution flaw in GitLab's regular-expression engine that the same researcher, who uses the handle joaxcar, has reported in a month, and the first to reach versions before 19.2.

On October 12, GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229, also an unauthenticated 10.0 overflow in the regex compiler, in versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, and 19.4.2. On September 23, it fixed two more, CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-89078, both rated 9.9 but requiring a logged-in account. The three earlier flaws stopped at version 19.2; this one does not.

The October 21 release fixes 11 security issues in all, one critical and the rest high, medium, or low.

Two of the others concern authentication. CVE-2026-15723, rated high at 8.2, could allow a logged-in user to take over another account, but only when an administrator has enabled both SAML and LDAP auto-linking.

A cache-poisoning flaw in GitLab's OAuth and OpenID Connect endpoints, CVE-2026-112212, rated high at 7.5, could allow an attacker to redirect certain sign-in flows to a server they control in setups that use a shared cache.

The upgrade carries a cost worth planning for. The 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 releases include database changes that run during the upgrade, and on a single-node server that means downtime while they finish. GitLab says multi-node setups can apply the patch without downtime using its zero-downtime procedure.

items.title: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
items.title_en: Enterprises keep buying software upgrades that IT thinks will make things worse
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Enterprise-sized businesses spend, on average, 28 percent of their software budgets on unwanted upgrades, migrations, and licensing changes. Often, those firms' IT heads think those changes are detrimental.

Those results are according to a survey of 2,018 chief information officers and senior IT decision-makers at companies with at least 10,000 employees that Origina commissioned for its report, “The Software Tax.” About half of the respondents (1,011) are from the US, and the rest are from the United Kingdom. All respondents worked at companies with at least $1 billion in annual revenue.

Keep in mind that Origina provides maintenance for various enterprise software. items.title: Mark Zuckerberg says Muse has drawn 10M+ users since its launch and 25%+ of users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of $200+ (Business Insider)
items.title_en: Mark Zuckerberg says Muse has drawn 10M+ users since its launch and 25%+ of users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of $200+ (Business Insider)
items.author: Business Insider
items.article_content:
Meta's new personal AI agent app has drawn more than 10 million users in the US and Canada since its September launch, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Wednesday.

During Meta's third-quarter earnings call, Zuckerberg said that Muse's growth "continues to be strong" and that the most common use case for the agent is shopping.

More than a quarter of Muse users are making purchases through the app, with an average purchase size of over $200, Zuckerberg said.

Beyond shopping, CFO Susan Li said on the call that Muse users most often use it for "personal productivity," connecting their email and calendars to the agent.

Meta's stock had surged after it released Muse. Its stock was up 5% after-hours on Wednesday.

The agent, which Meta says can help users handle tasks like sending an email or booking travel, quickly climbed to the top of Apple's App Store after its release, giving Zuckerberg an early win for his enormous AI spending.

Earlier on Wednesday, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for misleading users about how it handled their data and for failing to prevent misinformation on Facebook.

Move over, Facebook. Zuckerberg seems to have a new favorite product.

Want more Business Insider in your news feed?
                                  
                                    Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.

Add to Preferred Sources
                                  
                                
                              
                                    
                  
                  
                    
                  In Zuckerberg's opening remarks, he mentioned Muse nearly 50 times. Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp were only mentioned once.

"Muse went from an idea on a whiteboard to a successful product in just about eight months, and we're about to ship Muse Charm, which will have gone from concept to a hardware device in people's pockets in less than a year," Zuckerberg said on the call.

"I think that we are going to work on monetization somewhat sooner on this than our normal playbook for a couple of reasons," Zuckerberg said. "One is just the size of the numbers that we are talking about in terms of both the costs and the opportunity… make it important to make progress on that in order to be able to scale it."

The other reason, he said, is "such a large part of what people are doing is commerce."

Li added that Meta sees multiple paths to monetization, beginning with paid subscriptions. "We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses," she said.

Zuckerberg said Muse should remain free for most users, with Meta planning to make money from it through commerce tools that take a fee from transactions it helps facilitate.

He also said Muse is set to arrive on Meta's smart glasses next month, calling Muse "central to the business model for the glasses."

"We expect Muse and having your personal superintelligence with you throughout the day will be the most important part of the experience," he said.

Meanwhile, Forrester principal analyst Kate Winick said Wednesday that the biggest X-factor in Meta's AI ambitions is consumer trust.

"The more information Muse has, the more effective it can be, and overall trust in Meta remains low," Winick said.

She added, "But Meta has cultivated a reputation that negates trust as a condition for engagement: consumers almost expect to have their data mismanaged in exchange for a high level of connectivity and utility, and have shown that they're willing to keep showing up as long as the product experience delivers."

items.article_content_zh:
在三季度财报电话会议中，公司首席执行官向投资者披露，九月推出的个人智能体在北美市场上线后迅速积攒了超过一千万活跃用户。除了协助用户收发邮件和同步日程等日常办公生产力场景外，后台数据显示该应用最普遍、粘性最高的使用场景竟然是电商导购。不仅整体转化率超过百分之二十五，单笔平均订单金额更是突破了两百美元大关。

该产品的快速普及不仅助推其登顶苹果应用商店免费榜，也给近期持续承压的管理层打了一剂强心针。此前，由于在数据处理方式及虚假信息监管方面存在过失，公司刚刚遭遇法庭高额判罚；而这款主打个人助手的消费级应用在商业变现端的超预期表现，迅速提振了二级市场的信心，推动股价在盘后交易阶段逆势上扬。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在最新公布的三季度财报电话会议上，扎克伯格宣布旗下九月新推出的个人智能体应用在北美地区用户量已突破千万大关，并迅速登顶苹果应用商店榜首。数据显示该应用最核心的使用场景为购物，超过四分之一的用户直接在对话中完成下单，平均客单价突破两百美元。这一亮眼表现不仅为该公司此前遭受质疑的庞大技术资本支出提供了首个强力变现证据，也标志着其商业重心正向对话式电商深度转移。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: During the third-quarter earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg announced that Meta's new personal AI agent app Muse has drawn over 10 million users across the US and Canada since its September rollout, rapidly climbing to the top of the Apple App Store. Shopping has emerged as its primary use case, with over 25% of users completing transactions inside the app at an average purchase size exceeding $200. The strong momentum offers early commercial vindication for the company's aggressive AI capital expenditures while pivoting conversational interfaces into direct commerce funnels.

elements_zh.where: 公司第三季度财报业绩电话会议
elements_zh.what: 公布新推出的个人智能体应用用户突破千万，超两成半用户在此完成购物且平均客单价超两百美元，应用登顶苹果应用商店榜首
elements_zh.why: 向华尔街证明其巨额算力投入能够转化为高客单价的交易闭环，探索下一代社交电商入口

elements_en.what: Reported that the new personal AI agent reached 10M+ users with over 25% making purchases at a $200+ average basket size
elements_en.why: To demonstrate tangible commercial ROI on aggressive AI infrastructure spend by creating a conversational shopping funnel

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 兜兜转转这么多年，管理层终于想通了：别跟华尔街画通用人工智能的星辰大海，能在聊天框里把货卖出去才是硬道理。上一季还在被分析师追问几百亿芯片怎么回本，这头就把对话机器人硬生生做成了海外版带货窗口，连两百多美元的客单价都吹得有模有样。哪怕白天刚被法院开出天价数据罚单，只要财报里带货数据够诱人，资本市场立刻就能把前嫌忘得一干二净。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Tech giants have finally realized that abstract AGI dreams don't appease Wall Street—turning a chatbot into a high-ticket checkout counter does. After quarters of scrutiny over whether GPU spending would ever pay off, packaging conversational agents as frictionless digital personal shoppers makes the narrative instantly palatable. Even a massive regulatory penalty earlier that day couldn't spoil the post-earnings party once investors saw the lucrative transaction figures.

items.title: Meta expects its 2026 capex to be $135B-$145B, vs. $130B-$145B previously, and forecasts Q4 revenue of $73B-$76B, vs. $73.6B est.; META jumps 3%+ after hours (Riley Griffin/Bloomberg)
items.title_en: Meta expects its 2026 capex to be $135B-$145B, vs. $130B-$145B previously, and forecasts Q4 revenue of $73B-$76B, vs. $73.6B est.; META jumps 3%+ after hours (Riley Griffin/Bloomberg)
items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Riley Griffin / Bloomberg:
Meta expects its 2026 capex to be $135B-$145B, vs. $130B-$145B previously, and forecasts Q4 revenue of $73B-$76B, vs. $73.6B est.; META jumps 3%+ after hours  —  The Takeaways From Meta's Earnings and AI Spending Plans  —&nbsp
items.content_snippet: The Takeaways From Meta's Earnings and AI Spending Plans — Video Player is loading. — Unmute — Current Time 0:01 Loaded: 16.14% Playback Rate
items.summary_en: Meta updated its long-term financial guidance during its latest earnings release, raising the floor of its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to a staggering $135 billion to $145 billion. Simultaneously, management forecasted robust fourth-quarter revenues between $73 billion and $76 billion, comfortably beating consensus estimates of $73.6 billion. The figures reassured the market that resilient ad revenues can comfortably fund its relentless computing infrastructure buildout, lifting shares by over 3% in after-hours trading.
items.title_zh: 科技巨头上调后年资本支出上限至千亿美元规模
items.summary_zh: 社交与人工智能巨头在财报中上调资本开支指引并给出超预期营收展望，盘后股价上涨超百分之三
items.article_content_zh:
在最新公布的财务简报中，管理层大幅更新了对中长期资本支出的展望。即便此前市场已经对科技行业疯狂采购硬件的步伐有所预期，公司仍将未来年度的资本支出预期下限抬高至一千三百五十亿美元，上限维持在一千四百五十亿美元，明确释放出在下一代计算平台落成前绝不缩减算力基建的信号。

与巨额开支相匹配的是其表现强劲的基本面造血机制。公司预计第四季度整体营业收入将攀升至七百三十亿至七百六十亿美元区间，高于分析师平均预测的七百三十六亿美元。这种能够依靠现有广告生态持续变现以补足万亿级算力开销的财务结构，迅速缓解了投资者的抛售担忧，带动盘后股价反弹走高。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 社交网络与科技巨头在最新财报披露中调整了中长期财务预期，将两三年后的年度资本支出指引区间下限上调至一千三百五十亿至一千四百五十亿美元之间。同时，管理层给出了高达七百三十亿至七百六十亿美元的四季度营收指引，全面高于市场预期的七百三十六亿美元。这一组合拳表明其核心广告业务强劲的造血能力足以支撑无上限的算力基础设施扩建，刺激盘后股价应声上涨超过百分之三。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Meta updated its long-term financial guidance during its latest earnings release, raising the floor of its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to a staggering $135 billion to $145 billion. Simultaneously, management forecasted robust fourth-quarter revenues between $73 billion and $76 billion, comfortably beating consensus estimates of $73.6 billion. The figures reassured the market that resilient ad revenues can comfortably fund its relentless computing infrastructure buildout, lifting shares by over 3% in after-hours trading.

elements_zh.who: 科技跨国巨头财务与管理决策层
elements_zh.where: 季度财务报告发布及投资人业绩指引公告
elements_zh.what: 调高未来年度资本支出指引下限至上千亿美元高位，同时发布高于市场预期的四季度收入指引
elements_zh.why: 确立算力基建长期领先优势，并利用主营广告收入的现金流优势打消外界对资金断裂的担忧

elements_en.where: Quarterly earnings report and guidance update
elements_en.what: Lifted the 2026 capex projection floor to $135B-$145B and issued stronger-than-expected Q4 revenue guidance of $73B-$76B
elements_en.why: To secure long-term infrastructure dominance while proving that core advertising profits can sustain aggressive spending

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 只要主营广告这头现金奶牛还能挤出大把钞票，买芯片和建数据中心就根本不知道节制为何物。华尔街平时总爱忧心忡忡地敲黑板警告资本开支过热，可一旦看到下季度营收指引又超出预期，手指立刻诚实地把买入键按穿。千亿美元规模的算力豪赌表面上是科技理想，本质上是在用无法撼动的现金流优势筑起高墙，活活把后来者拖垮在算力成本的泥潭里。
ai_analysis.insight_en: As long as the core advertising cash cow keeps gushing profits, the leadership has zero intention of pumping the brakes on data center spending. Wall Street pretends to be terrified of runaway capex until quarterly revenue beats guidance, at which point algorithms immediately resume buying. Pouring well over a hundred billion dollars into infrastructure isn't just tech ambition; it's an economic siege designed to starve underfunded challengers out of the computational arms race.

The figures reassured the market that resilient ad revenues can comfortably fund its relentless computing infrastructure buildout, lifting shares by over 3% in after-hours trading.

items.title_en:
🚨 The AI gateway library LiteLLM was hijacked again in a supply chain attack.

It hid malware that runs whenever Python starts and steals SSH keys, cloud secrets and Claude Code configs.

It also raids LiteLLM's own database for every AI provider key stored. https://t.co/6nyAuaZmTM

items.title: RT @pushmeet: SynthID timeline over the last few weeks has been momentous – from opening SynthID Detector to the public,
items.title_en:
RT @pushmeet: SynthID timeline over the last few weeks has been momentous – from opening SynthID Detector to the public, to launching SynthID Bio to watermark functional, AI-designed proteins. 

Each moment brought us a step closer to our broader vision on provenance, or helping verify what is AI-generated and what isn’t.

Recently, Dartmouth Professor Hany Farid and I discussed why solving provenance is vital to @GoogleDeepMind’s broader mission to develop AI to benefit humanity.

In short: solving provenance is a highly complex, multi-disciplinary effort with watermarking technology at its core. It requires a collective mix of frontier research, interoperable open standards, and direct collaboration across platforms and developers.

Read our full conversation on Google's Public Policy blog: https://t.co/w8MEhnywKy

每一刻都让我们更接近我们对起源的更广泛的愿景，或者帮助验

items.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet, a proactive agent app on iOS, Android, and the web that works in the background, in research preview for US Pro and Max users (Claude)
items.title_en: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet, a proactive agent app on iOS, Android, and the web that works in the background, in research preview for US Pro and Max users (Claude)
items.author: Claude
items.article_content:
CategoryAnnouncementsDateOctober 21, 2026Reading time5 minShareCopy linkToday, we’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working even when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. We built Claude Duet for professionals and small business owners with more on their plates than they can track.

We designed Claude Duet to be a partner you can trust. Professionals of all kinds have to juggle many decisions a day, and we think they’ll find Claude Duet most useful. It helps you prioritize where to spend your time and energy, and to leave room for the ambitious projects that felt impossible or daunting before.

Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs your attention. You can also hand it tasks of all shapes—from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps.

Claude Duet draws on years of security, safety, and privacy work on agents, both our own and the infrastructure businesses use to run theirs:

How Duet handles sensitive information. We’re also releasing Claude Duet with a new dedicated classifier and safety system prompt that checks each message and guards against leaks of sensitive information. An agent that reads email and sends messages for you is constantly deciding where information should go. This new classifier and prompt are designed to reject requests to share the strictest tier of information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health or personal finances, are let through only when you’ve explicitly instructed Claude Duet to send it.

We’re continuing to develop and strengthen these protections, and will share more details about how Claude Duet is designed for safety in the coming days.

People at Anthropic have been using Claude Duet to accomplish more, but also to leave more room for thinking and being present. Boris Cherny, who leads our Claude Code team, talks through his mental to-do list with Claude Duet on walks, instead of saving the work for his desk. Chelsea Larsson, who leads our model and product behavior design team, hands Claude Duet her to-do list before leaving to be with her kids and it saves the results for an evening report. And the team behind Claude Duet uses it to build the product. Karan Ahuja, who leads the team, works with it to schedule user interviews, partner with him on prototypes, and even ship code.

We gave small business owners and entrepreneurs early access to Claude Duet, and some have been using it to help run their businesses. Here’s what some of them said:

Jess gets a rundown from Claude Duet each morning. One day, without being asked, it flagged a property showing that was on her calendar for the wrong day. “[This is] exactly the kind of thing I want caught without having to ask,” she said.

Amin owns Shahs of Kabob in South Florida with about 110 employees. He’s used Claude Duet for accounting, customer support, and marketing, and has worked through his invoices store by store. “It brings it all together,” he said. “I don’t need to open up 100 tabs.”

Mya had a call coming up with a potential client. Claude Duet saw it on her calendar and prepared a brief. It also noticed the call fell right before her flight and offered to move it. “I didn’t realize that it was right before my flight,” she said. “I love that proactivity.”

Your context from Claude is the foundation. Claude Duet carries over your memory, skills, and connected apps from your Claude account, so setting it up requires minimal work. What changes is how you work together: Claude Duet comes to you first, and you can message it through typing or voice in one ongoing thread, so a quick reply and a weeklong project both start in the same place.

Work continues when you step away. Claude Duet has a virtual machine with its own browser, so it doesn’t require your laptop or phone to be on. Describe a task in a short message, and it works out which apps to use and what steps to take in the background. You’ll receive a notification when the task is complete or needs your review.

Receive a message when something needs you. Claude Duet checks your connected accounts every few hours, because checking nonstop would use up your plan’s limits much faster. We’re continuing to test its judgment about when to message you, and we’ll keep tuning it based on what testers tell us. You can also tell it what you want to hear about and how often.

Important decisions stay with you. Claude Duet reads, drafts, and prepares work on its own. But before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your approval. A few things are off-limits even with your approval, like trading securities or moving money between accounts. You’re also able to disconnect any app Claude Duet has access to.

This is an early version of Claude Duet, and it still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what’s urgent. We built its core functionality around work, so personal errands, such as booking tickets, aren’t quite as strong, and it can’t yet show you its browser. For now, Claude Duet lives in its own app, separate from the main Claude app. What we learn from early users will shape how the two work together.

During the research preview, Claude Duet shares your plan’s usage limits with the rest of Claude, and it uses them differently than a typical conversation does. Its background checks count toward those limits, and larger tasks, like building a financial model or a deck, require more model turns and background work.

Explore more product news and best practices for teams building with Claude.

Available in public beta for Claude Enterprise customers.

items.summary_en: Anthropic has rolled out a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive autonomous agent application spanning iOS, Android, and web platforms for premium subscribers. Moving beyond passive question-and-answer chatbots, the agent runs continuously in the background across connected tools, compiling morning priority briefings and executing multi-step tasks while pinging users only when decisions or permissions are required. The initiative marks a strategic shift toward proactive digital co-workers capable of autonomously coordinating complex administrative workflows.
items.title_zh: 人工智能新星推出主动型后台智能体应用测试版
items.summary_zh: 大模型领军企业推出主动型智能体应用预览版，可在后台静默运行并跨多应用主动提醒与协同执行任务
items.article_content_zh:
该产品被定位于专业人士与中小企业经营者的全天候数字协同伙伴。与常见的对话式机器人不同，新版应用主打主动性和后台持续执行能力。每天清晨，应用会根据用户授权连接的多项工作软件，自动整合出亟待处理的重难点待办清单，并在整个工作日内保持静默追踪，仅在关键节点向用户请求授权或呈报异常。

在任务执行维度，该智能体支持从会议日程统筹等基础行政事务，跨越到复杂的数据仪表盘搭建、销售预测建模乃至基础原型开发。团队在设计中强调了安全边界，任何涉及替用户采取不可逆操作的行为，均必须获得用户的显式确认，以此在自动化效能与操作可控性之间寻找平衡。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知名大模型创新团队正式上线了一款名为主动副驾的全新智能体应用研究预览版，同步覆盖移动设备与网页端。该应用突破了传统一问一答的交互模式，能够在系统后台持续静默运行，主动抓取所关联工作软件的上下文并向用户推送早报，只有在关键决议或需要核准操作时才会主动发起打扰。此举旨在将大模型从被动应答的虚拟顾问转变为能够主动代办跨平台复杂日程的数字化办公协作者。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Anthropic has rolled out a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive autonomous agent application spanning iOS, Android, and web platforms for premium subscribers. Moving beyond passive question-and-answer chatbots, the agent runs continuously in the background across connected tools, compiling morning priority briefings and executing multi-step tasks while pinging users only when decisions or permissions are required. The initiative marks a strategic shift toward proactive digital co-workers capable of autonomously coordinating complex administrative workflows.

elements_zh.who: 大模型独角兽产品研发团队
elements_zh.where: 官方多端应用上架与产品功能预览发布场景
elements_zh.what: 发布能够在后台自主运行的主动型智能体应用，支持晨间简报汇总、任务后台托管与跨软件协作
elements_zh.why: 打破聊天框界面的被动交互局限，争夺职场专业人士深度绑定的下一代操作系统级工作入口

elements_en.who: Leading AI research and product team
elements_en.where: Official product launch across mobile and web platforms
elements_en.what: Introduced a proactive background agent app that sends prioritized briefs, monitors apps, and executes tasks semi-autonomously
elements_en.why: To transcend passive conversational interfaces and capture the high-value workflow entry point for professionals

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 从你问一句它答一句的呆板客服，终于进化成了自己默默干活、有事再来拍你肩膀的资深打工人。不过后台随时盯着你全套工作软件并主动发消息，表面上听起来是无微不至的贴身数字管家，实际压迫感直接拉满。一旦连做报表、排日程和催进度都全自动化了，打工人以后上班摸鱼可就真没有任何借口了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Chatbots have finally evolved from reactive assistants into seasoned corporate operators that work quietly in the background and only tap your shoulder when an approval is due. But having an AI constantly surveying all your enterprise software to assign you daily priorities sounds less like liberation and more like an infallible digital micro-manager. Once the machine proactively schedules meetings and builds dashboards for you, blaming administrative chaos for missed deadlines is officially off the table.

ai_analysis.digest_en: Anthropic has rolled out a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive autonomous agent application spanning iOS, Android, and web platforms for premium subscribers. Moving beyond passive question-and-answer chatbots, the agent runs continuously in the background across connected tools, compiling morning priority briefings and executing multi-step tasks while pinging users only when decisions or permissions are required. The initiative marks a strategic shift toward proactive digital co-workers capable of autonomously coordinating complex administrative workflows.

items.author: OpenAI 官方动态
items.original_content: How OpenAI works with distribution partners to uphold consistent safeguards, support responsible access, and clarify expectations in our Usage Policies.
items.content_snippet: How OpenAI works with distribution partners to uphold consistent safeguards, support responsible access, and clarify expectations in our Usage Policies.
items.summary_en: OpenAI published updated ecosystem guidance outlining consistent security standards and usage policies for its global distribution partners. The framework mandates that downstream distributors and solution providers adhere to identical baseline safety guardrails and responsible access requirements when integrating and reselling foundational models. The move is designed to mitigate escalating regulatory liabilities from widespread distribution while tightening centralized control across its expanding developer ecosystem.
items.title_zh: 行业龙头明确全球渠道合作统一安全准则与使用规范
items.summary_zh: 领先技术机构面向全球分销合作伙伴出台统一安全规范，明确合规接入底线与生态治理要求
items.article_content_zh: 该份规范文件重点阐明了源头模型提供方如何与全球分销商协同落地安全防线的细则。随着大模型能力被越来越多地嵌入企业级应用、云服务商平台及第三方行业解决方案，如何防止模型能力在二次开发中被滥用成为了监管层重点关注的焦点。新出台的指引对各类下游接入方在调用频率、敏感领域过滤和最终用户审计等方面提出了更为细致的刚性要求。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 大模型行业领航机构在其最新官方生态指引中，正式明确了与全球分销伙伴的统一安全防线与使用规范。文件要求所有下游渠道商在分发底层技术和提供服务接口时，必须严格贯彻一致的安全防护机制与滥用防御措施，确保技术在多层级转售场景下仍符合既定规则。此举旨在应对伴随渠道扩张而激增的法律与合规风险，同时进一步巩固核心厂商对整个应用生态的绝对主导权。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI published updated ecosystem guidance outlining consistent security standards and usage policies for its global distribution partners. The framework mandates that downstream distributors and solution providers adhere to identical baseline safety guardrails and responsible access requirements when integrating and reselling foundational models. The move is designed to mitigate escalating regulatory liabilities from widespread distribution while tightening centralized control across its expanding developer ecosystem.

elements_zh.where: 官方技术生态治理与使用政策发布场景
elements_zh.what: 发布针对全球渠道分销伙伴的统一安全保障准则，明晰使用政策边界与合规责任划分
elements_zh.why: 应对多层级技术分发引发的安全失控隐患，在满足全球监管要求的同时强化对下游渠道的治理约束

elements_en.who: Policy and ecosystem compliance teams at a leading AI lab
elements_en.where: Official policy declaration and developer portal
elements_en.what: Issued uniform safety safeguards and usage policies binding global distribution partners to consistent compliance standards
elements_en.why: To curb safety loopholes across downstream distribution chains and satisfy global regulatory scrutiny while retaining ecosystem control

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 翻译一下就是：想靠分销我的模型吃红利可以，但所有绳套都得按我的尺寸来戴。把加强渠道控制和法律免责切割精心包装成负责任开放的行业担当，既给随时准备找茬的监管部门递上了合规投名状，又顺理成章地给下游所有转售商戴上了金箍。生态繁荣的大旗由它来扛，安全违规的黑锅由分销商去背，这套公关太极打得确实滴水不漏。
ai_analysis.insight_en: In plain terms: you are welcome to make a profit reselling the frontier models, but every leash remains firmly held by the provider. Packaging channel control and liability protection as an altruistic commitment to global safety standards is PR at its finest. It satisfies anxious regulators with ready-made compliance paperwork while ensuring that if an edge case goes haywire, downstream resellers will be the ones taking the blame.

items.original_content:
Pierre Paulden / Bloomberg:
Filing: Meta says Mark Zuckerberg is considering leaving California if it passes a one-time 5% tax on billionaires; voters will decide on the measure next month  —  Mark Zuckerberg said he is considering leaving California if it passes
items.content_snippet: Mark Zuckerberg said he is considering leaving California if it passes a measure that would impose a one-time, 5% tax on billionaires.
items.summary_en: Mark Zuckerberg disclosed in a regulatory filing that he is considering leaving California if the state passes a proposed one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires in next month's ballot. The measure, which California voters will soon decide on, faces stiff resistance from Silicon Valley leaders seeking to protect their assets. The move underscores growing tensions between tech elites and progressive tax policies in the state.
items.title_zh: 文件：Meta表示，如果加州通过对亿万富翁一次性征收5%的税，马克·扎克伯格将考虑离开加州；选民将在下个月就这项措施作出决定。

items.title: Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027 (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
items.title_en: Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027 (Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal)
items.author: Wall Street Journal
items.original_content:
Meghan Bobrowsky / Wall Street Journal:
Meta says it will create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise the capital it needs for developing AI models, with an effective date in January 2027  —  The company, which reported record revenue of $64.2 billion for the t
items.content_snippet: The company, which reported record revenue of $64.2 billion for the third quarter, said the new stock won't affect Mark Zuckerberg's voting control
items.summary_en: Meta announced the establishment of a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, scheduled to become effective in January 2027, to finance its aggressive AI model development. The structure enables the company to raise massive public capital for AI infrastructure without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's absolute voting control. The strategic move comes as generative AI training demands unprecedented capital expenditure.
items.title_zh: Meta表示，它将创建一种新的无投票权股票，以筹集开发人工智能模型所需的资金，该股票将于2027年1月生效。
items.summary_zh: Meghan Bobrowsky/Wall Street Journal ： Meta表示，它将创建一类新的无表决权股票，以筹集开发人工智能模型所需的资金，有效期为2027年1月— The com

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta在季度财报披露中宣布将设立全新的无投票权C类普通股，该机制计划于2027年1月正式生效。此举旨在为日益膨胀的AI基础模型研发与基础设施采购筹集充裕的资本，同时避免稀释扎克伯格及创始团队的控制权。随着算力军备竞赛白热化，Meta试图在维持独揽大权的前提下向资本市场大举借力。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Meta announced the establishment of a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, scheduled to become effective in January 2027, to finance its aggressive AI model development. The structure enables the company to raise massive public capital for AI infrastructure without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's absolute voting control. The strategic move comes as generative AI training demands unprecedented capital expenditure.

elements_zh.what: 设立全新无投票权C类普通股筹资用于AI大模型研发，2027年1月生效
elements_zh.why: 筹集天量AI算力基建资金，同时防止创始团队投票控制权被稀释

elements_en.where: Corporate earnings release and governance filings
elements_en.what: Creating a new class of nonvoting common stock effective January 2027 for AI funding
elements_en.why: To fund massive AI capital expenditures without diluting founder voting control

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 扎克伯格给华尔街上了一堂生动的算盘课：买英伟达芯片的钱你们来出，但是公司的决策权你们休想碰哪怕一丝一毫。所谓‘无投票权股票’翻译过来就是：闭嘴掏钱买算力，看小扎继续在AI牌桌上豪赌。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Zuckerberg's message to Wall Street is delightfully transparent: please bankroll our multi-billion-dollar GPU addiction, but don't you dare ask for a seat at the table. Nonvoting shares simply mean 'shut up, fund our AI models, and let Zuck play dictator in peace.'
ai_analysis.digest_zh: Meta在季度财报披露中宣布将设立全新的无投票权C类普通股，该机制计划于2027年1月正式生效。此举旨在为日益膨胀的AI基础模型研发与基础设施采购筹集充裕的资本，同时避免稀释扎克伯格及创始团队的控制权。随着算力军备竞赛白热化，Meta试图在维持独揽大权的前提下向资本市场大举借力。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Meta announced the establishment of a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, scheduled to become effective in January 2027, to finance its aggressive AI model development. The structure enables the company to raise massive public capital for AI infrastructure without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's absolute voting control. The strategic move comes as generative AI training demands unprecedented capital expenditure.
key_points_zh: Meta正式宣布创设全新无投票权股票类别
新股机制计划于2027年1月正式落地生效
核心动机为AI基础设施与大模型研发筹措长期充沛弹药
key_points_en: Meta establishes new nonvoting Class C common stock
Structure is scheduled to take effect in January 2027
Aimed at financing massive compute needs while safeguarding governance control

items.title_en: Meta reports Q3 revenue up 26% YoY to $64.6B, operating income down 37% to $12.99B on a $9.89B AG settlement charge, and family DAP up 3% to 3.64B for September (Meta)
items.author: Meta
items.original_content:
Meta:
Meta reports Q3 revenue up 26% YoY to $64.6B, operating income down 37% to $12.99B on a $9.89B AG settlement charge, and family DAP up 3% to 3.64B for September  —  Announces Establishment of New Class C Common Stock  —  Meta Platforms, Inc.
items.content_snippet: Announces Establishment of New Class C Common Stock — Meta Platforms, Inc. (Nasdaq: META) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
items.summary_en: Meta reported Q3 revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year, while daily active people across its app family reached 3.64 billion. However, operating income plunged 37% to $12.99 billion, heavily dragged down by an extraordinary $9.89 billion state attorney general settlement charge. The results show durable core advertising momentum masked by hefty, one-time regulatory clearing costs.

items.title_en:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just launched Duet, its always-on personal agent. It’s the first personal agent I’d call a pro tool.

We’ve been testing it for two weeks. I’ve gone from mostly using ChatGPT to roughly 50/50 between ChatGPT and Claude—the most time I’ve spent with Anthropic in close to a year.

• It lives in its own app, separate from Claude, on iOS, Android, and the web. This makes it feel clean and easy to understand.
• It has channels for specific areas of your work and life rather than just a single chat
• It has a todo list so you never lose what you’re working on and you can always see statuses
• It allows you to easily write and edit documents, slides, and more all through the app.
• It’s not a chief of staff yet. It can see the Claude sessions on my computers but can’t direct them. Its email drafts are worse than dot’s, and voice is transcription only—you can’t have a spoken conversation with it.

My verdict: the vibes are good, and I’m opening Duet every day. It’s worth trying.

Check out our agent comparison page: https://t.co/fZyTorNK4p

Full Vibe Check coming soon on @every

items.title:
If I had 6 months to become a Software Architect in the AI era.

I’d do this.

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: Wha
items.title_en:
If I had 6 months to become a Software Architect in the AI era.

I’d do this.

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: What architecture is, Architect vs Senior vs Tech Lead, quality attributes, functional vs non-functional requirements, stakeholders & constraints.

- Practice: Map quality attributes & conflicting drivers for one real system.

- Why: AI writes code. Architects decide what must not change when stakeholders and constraints shift.

STAGE 2: Architectural Thinking

- Learn: Tradeoffs, ADRs, fitness functions, technical debt, Conway’s Law.

- Practice: Write 5 ADRs & define fitness functions that reject bad designs.

- Why: AI proposes options. You own the recorded decision & its long-term cost.

STAGE 3: Design Principles

- Learn: SOLID, cohesion/coupling, boundaries, dependency inversion, YAGNI/KISS, complexity budget.

- Practice: Refactor a coupled service into ports & adapters under a hard complexity limit.

- Why: Generated code grows fast. Principles keep boundaries intact so change stays local.

STAGE 4: Styles & Patterns

- Learn: Modular monolith, microservices, hexagonal/clean, event-driven, CQRS & event sourcing.

- Practice: Implement one feature three ways & measure operational differences.

- Why: No single style wins. You choose & evolve the pattern that matches team size and change rate.

STAGE 5: Domain Modeling

- Learn: Strategic DDD, bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, anti-corruption layer.

- Practice: Model a domain with two teams + one AI agent and add an anti-corruption boundary.

- Why: AI multiplies features. Clear contexts stop the domain from becoming inconsistent.

STAGE 6: Data & Persistence

- Learn: Data ownership, SQL vs NoSQL, partitioning, sagas/outbox, polyglot persistence.

- Practice: Design ownership boundaries + outbox for a system that mixes relational and vector data.

- Why: Agents write data. Ownership and consistency rules prevent silent corruption.

STAGE 7: Distributed Systems

- Learn: CAP/PACELC, consistency models, failure modes, idempotency, fallacies of distribution.

- Practice: Simulate partitions and show safe retries with an explicit consistency choice.

- Why: AI calls are multi-hop and async. You design for the failures generated code ignores.

STAGE 8: Integration & APIs

- Learn: Sync vs async, contracts & versioning, choreography vs orchestration, gateways.

- Practice: Build a versioned contract plus hybrid sync/async flow that includes agent steps.

- Why: Agents call constantly. Stable contracts and the right orchestration keep the system evolvable.

STAGE 9: Evolution & Production

- Learn: Evolutionary architecture, observability, SLIs/SLOs, resilience patterns, least privilege.

- Practice: Strangle one module, add full traces including agent calls & set error budgets.

- Why: Systems change while agents run. You keep production stable under continuous autonomous activity.

STAGE 10: Practice & Communication

- Learn: C4 diagrams, ADRs, architecture katas, classic system cases.

- Practice: Produce a full C4 + ADR set and publish one bottleneck teardown.

- Why: Architects are hired for judgment and clear decisions that survive teams, scale, and AI-driven change.

CRUD is dead. AI writes the boilerplate.

The "modern architect" builds the decision system that stays coherent under change, teams & autonomous agents.

Bookmark & RT!

items.full_text_en:
If I had 6 months to become a Software Architect in the AI era.

I’d do this.

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: What architecture is, Architect vs Senior vs Tech Lead, quality attributes, functional vs non-functional requirements, stakeholders & constraints.

- Practice: Map quality attributes & conflicting drivers for one real system.

- Why: AI writes code. Architects decide what must not change when stakeholders and constraints shift.

STAGE 2: Architectural Thinking

- Learn: Tradeoffs, ADRs, fitness functions, technical debt, Conway’s Law.

- Practice: Write 5 ADRs & define fitness functions that reject bad designs.

- Why: AI proposes options. You own the recorded decision & its long-term cost.

STAGE 3: Design Principles

- Learn: SOLID, cohesion/coupling, boundaries, dependency inversion, YAGNI/KISS, complexity budget.

- Practice: Refactor a coupled service into ports & adapters under a hard complexity limit.

- Why: Generated code grows fast. Principles keep boundaries intact so change stays local.

STAGE 4: Styles & Patterns

- Learn: Modular monolith, microservices, hexagonal/clean, event-driven, CQRS & event sourcing.

- Practice: Implement one feature three ways & measure operational differences.

- Why: No single style wins. You choose & evolve the pattern that matches team size and change rate.

STAGE 5: Domain Modeling

- Learn: Strategic DDD, bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, anti-corruption layer.

- Practice: Model a domain with two teams + one AI agent and add an anti-corruption boundary.

- Why: AI multiplies features. Clear contexts stop the domain from becoming inconsistent.

STAGE 6: Data & Persistence

- Learn: Data ownership, SQL vs NoSQL, partitioning, sagas/outbox, polyglot persistence.

- Practice: Design ownership boundaries + outbox for a system that mixes relational and vector data.

- Why: Agents write data. Ownership and consistency rules prevent silent corruption.

STAGE 7: Distributed Systems

- Learn: CAP/PACELC, consistency models, failure modes, idempotency, fallacies of distribution.

- Practice: Simulate partitions and show safe retries with an explicit consistency choice.

- Why: AI calls are multi-hop and async. You design for the failures generated code ignores.

STAGE 8: Integration & APIs

- Learn: Sync vs async, contracts & versioning, choreography vs orchestration, gateways.

- Practice: Build a versioned contract plus hybrid sync/async flow that includes agent steps.

- Why: Agents call constantly. Stable contracts and the right orchestration keep the system evolvable.

STAGE 9: Evolution & Production

- Learn: Evolutionary architecture, observability, SLIs/SLOs, resilience patterns, least privilege.

- Practice: Strangle one module, add full traces including agent calls & set error budgets.

- Why: Systems change while agents run. You keep production stable under continuous autonomous activity.

STAGE 10: Practice & Communication

- Learn: C4 diagrams, ADRs, architecture katas, classic system cases.

- Practice: Produce a full C4 + ADR set and publish one bottleneck teardown.

- Why: Architects are hired for judgment and clear decisions that survive teams, scale, and AI-driven change.

CRUD is dead. AI writes the boilerplate.

The "modern architect" builds the decision system that stays coherent under change, teams & autonomous agents.

items.title_en:
PSA: in light of recent cyberattacks and vulnerabilities, I recommend everyone:

* use a good password manager (1Password) and do not duplicate passwords 
* use two factor auth for everything important (not via sms!! Google Authenticator or better yet YubiKey)
* Auto-updates on, and restart weekly so they actually install
* Freeze your credit
* Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN
* Get your cell carrier to give you a port-out PIN or number lock that makes the carrier refuse to move your number without the PIN

You can ask your claude code to audit what on your laptop is out of date and needs updating.

items.original_content:
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol discovered a critical PHP vulnerability as part of the Patch the Planet initiative that could affect millions of websites. Security firm Wiz independently found the same flaw using Google's Gemini 4 Argon. OpenAI warns that the same AI capabilities that find vulnerabilities can help attackers too.

The article OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites appeared first on The Decoder.
items.content_snippet:
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol discovered a critical PHP vulnerability as part of the Patch the Planet initiative that could affect millions of websites. Security firm Wiz independently found the same flaw using Google's Gemini 4 Argon. OpenAI warns that the same AI capabilities that find vulnerabilities can help attackers too.

The article OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon found critical PHP flaw affecting millions of websites appeared first on The Decoder.
items.summary_en: Next-generation models from OpenAI and Google independently uncovered a critical PHP vulnerability that threatens millions of public websites worldwide. The flaw was independently verified through security firm Wiz during ecosystem testing. OpenAI simultaneously warned that the advanced reasoning enabling this discovery could also arm malicious threat actors with automated cyberattack capabilities.
items.title_zh: OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol和谷歌的Gemini 4 Argon发现了影响数百万网站的关键PHP漏洞
items.summary_zh: OpenAI与谷歌的大模型分别独立挖掘出影响数百万站点的PHP高危漏洞，同时引发攻防失衡担忧

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI旗下的最新模型与谷歌的下一代大模型在独立安全测试中，先后挖出了一项波及全球数百万网站的底层PHP关键严重漏洞。安全机构通过双向交叉验证确认了该漏洞的危害性。然而研发团队同时发出严正警告：展现出此等神级挖洞能力的大模型一旦被恶意逆向使用，也将以同样毁灭性的效率辅助黑客实施全自动渗透攻击。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Next-generation models from OpenAI and Google independently uncovered a critical PHP vulnerability that threatens millions of public websites worldwide. The flaw was independently verified through security firm Wiz during ecosystem testing. OpenAI simultaneously warned that the advanced reasoning enabling this discovery could also arm malicious threat actors with automated cyberattack capabilities.

elements_en.who: OpenAI, Google, and security researchers at Wiz
elements_en.where: Global infrastructure open-source code vulnerability auditing
elements_en.what: Independently identified a severe PHP exploit impacting millions of domains
elements_en.why: AI code reasoning excels at vulnerability hunting, but exposes dual-use offensive risks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 这波属于‘矛与盾都掌握在同一帮AI手里’。最讽刺的是，AI不仅比最资深的代码审计专家更能挑刺，连发出的免责警告都一模一样：‘我能救你，但坏人拿我去杀你我也拦不住’。留给那些多年不修老旧代码的站长们的安稳觉，恐怕真不多了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: AI just automated white-hat bug bounties and black-hat exploit development at the exact same time. The irony is unmistakable: the same system fixing your legacy code could just as easily hand-craft a zero-day exploit for script kiddies. Legacy webmasters officially have zero excuses left.

items.title_en:
highly recommend everyone to have private alt accounts*. the x web is bad at account switching, but on mobile it is frictionless. its basically the same "group chat but its ok if you dont read everything" experience but for your mutuals.

tips
- assume everything is public, screenshotting is real, dont be stupid. this is not the "i shit talk people behind their back", the right attitude is "this isnt high signal enough for my main account but i'm 1) taking notes for self, 2) have a throwaway thought, 3) i'm happy to chat about it"
- give mutuals critical feedback that they might appreciate. "praise in public, criticise in private". because its not public, they know you actually do mean well
- link/replyguy your alt for people to discover periodicially in case they dont know you have one

* i like it so much that i call this the "insta/finsta" pattern - every social network should by default give people a public profile and a private one by default. tbd on the third account, the "botsta".

items.title: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you
items.title_en: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Walmart will soon let AI agents shop on its website for you. Next month, the retail giant will allow you to connect your own AI agent to the site, with systems in place to let you approve and review purchases and set spending limits.

The embrace of AI agents stands in stark contrast to Amazon, which blocked Perplexity's shopping agent and Meta's Muse AI assistant. But Walmart is opening its doors to AI shoppers - as long as they follow the retailer's rules. It has outlined a set of terms for agents, saying that "agents must not take actions beyond what the shopper intends" and cannot change a customer's payment method. Agents also can only  …

items.summary_en: Walmart announced plans to permit customers to link personal AI agents directly to its e-commerce platform starting next month, enabling automated shopping within strict spending limits and manual review gates. The retailer laid out clear boundary guidelines to prevent unauthorized payment modifications and out-of-scope actions. The welcoming approach directly counters Amazon's hostile strategy of aggressively banning third-party shopping agents.
items.title_zh: 沃尔玛正在邀请人工智能代理为你购物
items.summary_zh: 沃尔玛下月起允许第三方AI智能体直接接入代客下单购物，与亚马逊的筑墙封杀策略大相径庭

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 沃尔玛宣布将于下月起正式开放电商接口，允许消费者接入自主选择的第三方AI智能体在其官方网站代为选购并提交订单。平台为此设立了审核把关、预算限额及支付方式锁定等安全护栏，并明令禁止智能体越权操作。这一极度开放的态度与全面封锁竞品AI爬虫与导购助手的亚马逊形成鲜明对立，旨在借助外部AI流量抢占下一代智能零售入口。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Walmart announced plans to permit customers to link personal AI agents directly to its e-commerce platform starting next month, enabling automated shopping within strict spending limits and manual review gates. The retailer laid out clear boundary guidelines to prevent unauthorized payment modifications and out-of-scope actions. The welcoming approach directly counters Amazon's hostile strategy of aggressively banning third-party shopping agents.

elements_zh.where: 全球数字零售与电商平台接口策略发布
elements_zh.what: 下月起全面支持用户自选AI智能体代客在官网下单购物，并设定合规协议规则
elements_zh.why: 与亚马逊的闭门防守形成差异化竞争，争夺智能体时代的电商流量与购物入口

elements_en.where: Global digital retail and web platform deployment
elements_en.what: Allowing customer AI agents to autonomously shop online under defined behavioral constraints
elements_en.why: Countering Amazon's walled-garden approach to capture early autonomous AI commerce traffic

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当亚马逊还在把AI当成盗窃流量的‘网购小偷’严防死守时，沃尔玛已经想通了：管你是人是硅基生物，只要带着钱包来结账就是好顾客。给AI设置花钱限额不仅显得极具前瞻性，还能顺手把‘帮用户管好AI钱包’的护城河给占了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: While Amazon treats incoming shopping bots like digital shoplifters to be banned on sight, Walmart simply asks: does the robot have a valid credit card? Welcoming autonomous shoppers with strict spending collars is both savvy opportunism and a masterclass in hijacking next-gen AI retail traffic.

items.title_en:
AI agents are writing more code. How can developers ensure that code is correct?

Microsoft Research’s Proof-Driven Development (PDD) Kit explores a more rigorous approach: it translates a developer’s intent into a formal specification, then uses formal verification to prove that generated code meets it.

PDD Kit works with Verus for Rust and is integrated with @GitHubNext’s Chopin, bringing formal methods into an AI-assisted development workflow for teams.

See the work in action at @github Universe, Oct. 28–29, 2026.

items.title_en:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash + SGLang Omni: building toward a more interactive generation of voice agents. The shift ahead is from “ask, wait, listen” to conversations people can interrupt, correct, and redirect as a task unfolds.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash brings intelligence and fast, concise responses. SGLang Omni adds streaming, conversation state, and interruption handling so users can redirect conversations in real time.

Together, they give developers a foundation to explore proactive tutors, support agents, and hands-free copilots - pairing Flash’s capabilities with infrastructure for continuous interaction.

Thanks to the SGLang Omni team for exploring this direction with M3.1 Flash! ✨

items.title: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99 (Tom Warren/The Verge)
items.title_en: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99 (Tom Warren/The Verge)
items.author: The Verge
items.article_content:
GamingCloseGamingPosts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.

Microsoft is opening up Xbox Cloud Gaming to anyone in November.

Tom WarrenCloseTom WarrenSenior CorrespondentPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ShareGiftIllustration by Alex Castro / The VergeTom WarrenCloseTom WarrenPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Xbox Insiders who don’t have a Game Pass subscription will be able to start purchasing cloud playtime today, ahead of a broader rollout next month. Insiders can access “introductory” launch pricing bundles:

All of these cloud hours will include ad-free cloud gaming, shorter wait times, and higher-quality streaming. These aren’t monthly bundles of hours either, so once you purchased a pack it remains available until the hours are used.

The pay-as-you-go Xbox Cloud Gaming option arrives just in time for Grand Theft Auto VI. I reported earlier this month that Microsoft has secured Grand Theft Auto VI streaming rights, but it’s not yet clear if this will be limited to just Xbox consoles. Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft won’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI to PCs, suggesting that the web browsers and apps that can usually access Xbox Cloud Gaming will not be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI.

Microsoft also continues to test free, ad-supported cloud gaming for Xbox Insiders, offering up another way to stream games without Game Pass. The free streaming sessions are limited to games you already own, and sessions are capped at one hour.

items.summary_en: Microsoft is officially decoupling Xbox Cloud Gaming from its mandatory Game Pass monthly subscription by launching standalone, pay-as-you-go hourly playtime bundles. Rolling out to Xbox Insiders today and broad consumers next month, packages are priced from $3.99 for 10 hours up to $11.99 for 50 hours with no monthly expiration. The model seeks to lure casual gamers looking for flexibility ahead of massive upcoming blockbuster game releases.
items.title_zh: Microsoft reveals pricing for Xbox Cloud Gaming without Game Pass, for Xbox Insiders now and others next month: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, 50 for $11.99
items.summary_zh: 微软Xbox云游戏面向非订阅会员推出按小时计费模式，低至3.99美元即可享受免广告高画质串流

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软宣布全面打破Xbox云游戏此前必须捆绑Game Pass月度会员订阅的限制，正式推出按时长计费的独立游玩套餐。该方案即日起向内测玩家开放，下月推向所有用户，定价为10小时3.99美元、25小时7.99美元及50小时11.99美元。购买的时长包无过期作废限制，并承诺提供免广告、超低延迟等待和最高流媒体画质，意在降低高门槛、吸引非核心玩家在重磅大作发售周期内灵活消费。

elements_zh.why: 降低云游戏尝试门槛，迎战重磅新游戏周期并拓宽非包月订阅用户的变现渠道

elements_en.where: Official platform feature and pricing announcement
elements_en.what: Introduced non-subscription hourly playtime bundles starting at $3.99 without monthly expiration
elements_en.why: To lower entry friction for casual gamers ahead of major releases and monetize non-subscribers

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 兜兜转转几十年，云游戏终究还是活成了‘赛博网吧’按小时开机充值的模样。虽然按时计费被包装成了永不过期的普惠套餐，但本质上还是因为发现每个月固定交月费的冤大头不够用了，赶紧把只想体验几把大作的散客也网罗进来吸干零钱。
ai_analysis.insight_en: After decades of hyping the post-console streaming revolution, cloud gaming has essentially reinvented the 90s cybercafe hourly punch card. When you realize you've tapped out monthly recurring subscribers, pitching 'pay-as-you-go packs' is the classic pivot to extract loose pocket change from casual tourists.

items.title_en:
there's a big opportunity in AI advisory right now, a gap in the market that's waiting to be filled...

atm there are two types of "AI experts":

the AI normie
- know how to use tools but completely delegate his thinking
- don't think in systems
- can't implement AI in real business workflows

the full AI nerd
- know everything there's to know about AI
- has 10 Claude Code instances running his life
- can't communicate with an human

and this is where YOUR opportunity is...

the market is screaming for a third type: the AI advisor

someone who can walk into a business, look at their operations for 2 hours, and say "this process right here? AI cuts it by 40% and here's exactly how"

they're looking for that guy who's deep enough in the rabbit hole to fix their problems, but also smart enough to dumb things down so they can understand the solution

be that guy

items.title: Someone developed an app that purportedly removes AI content from your feed, and it has been revealed that it was create
items.title_en:
Someone developed an app that purportedly removes AI content from your feed, and it has been revealed that it was created using AI vibe coding. 

The detector also uses "AI" to detect AI art content...

Oh, the Irony... It flags, classifies, and hides AI art using entirely AI-based context detection with an open source LLM called Gemma. 

The funny thing is that AI detection of AI content using LLMs is very inaccurate, with a lot of false positives and negatives.
items.title_zh:
有人开发了一款应用程序，据称可以从你的feed中删除人工智能内容，据透露，这款应用程序是使用人工智能vibe编码创建的。

检测器还使用“AI”来检测AI美术内容……

哦，讽刺的是……它使用完全基于AI的上下文检测来标记、分类和隐藏AI图

Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation  —  Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised
items.content_snippet: Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised $1 billion in funding at a $6 billion valuation …
items.summary_en: One-year-old AI startup Flapping Airplanes has secured $1 billion in fresh capital, catapulting its valuation to $6 billion. The company develops algorithmic and architectural innovations that slash training data requirements, reduce compute bottlenecks, and optimize chip efficiency. The colossal funding highlights urgent investor appetite for alternatives to brutal brute-force GPU scaling amidst skyrocketing infrastructure bills.
items.title_zh: Flapping Airplanes, which is working on methods to train AI models using less data and compute and make the chips more efficient, raised $1B at a $6B valuation
items.summary_zh: 主打低算力少数据训练AI的初创公司成立仅一年即斩获10亿美元融资，估值飙升至60亿美元

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 成立仅一年的低算力算法与芯片优化初创公司Flapping Airplanes宣布完成10亿美元的新一轮巨额融资，公司投后估值一举冲上60亿美元。该企业致力于打破盲目堆砌海量数据与万卡集群的暴力训练范式，专注研发能以极少数据和算力训练高能效大模型的新型软硬件协同技术。其在资本市场引发的抢投潮，折射出顶级风投在昂贵的算力重负之下，正极力寻找能降本增效的颠覆性底层技术。

The colossal funding highlights urgent investor appetite for alternatives to brutal brute-force GPU scaling amidst skyrocketing infrastructure bills.

When everyone is bleeding billions paying the Nvidia GPU tax, the mere promise of making AI training cheaper will have venture capitalists racing to dump dump-trucks of cash at your doorstep.

Google Cloud is the first major cloud provider to offer Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI's GPTs on a single platform. At launch, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna are available as a private preview for enterprise customers.

items.summary_zh: 谷歌云平台宣布在其平台上同步提供Gemini、Claude及OpenAI模型，成为首家集齐三大主流AI巨头的云服务商

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌云平台宣布在其平台上同步提供Gemini、Claude及OpenAI模型，成为首家集齐三大主流AI巨头的云服务商。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google Cloud has integrated OpenAI models alongside Gemini and Claude into its enterprise platform, becoming the first major cloud provider to offer all three top-tier AI families in one place to meet diverse enterprise demands.

elements_zh.where: 企业级云服务平台
elements_zh.what: 宣布在平台上同时提供Gemini、Claude与OpenAI模型，并向企业客户开放私有预览。
elements_zh.why: 为了打破模型阵营壁垒，一站式满足企业客户调度不同顶尖AI的业务需求。

elements_en.what: Offered Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI models simultaneously on a single platform with private preview for enterprises.
elements_en.why: To break model silos and meet enterprises' growing demands for a one-stop multi-model hub.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大模型军备战打成了“全家桶大乱炖”，谷歌云这是主打一个“不管你粉哪家AI，终究都得给我交云费”。什么叫格局？这就是把死敌请进自家客厅还能顺便收个全屋物业费的资本艺术。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When AI wars turn into a buffet, Google Cloud proves that you don't need to win the model race if you can just charge rent to all your rivals living under your roof.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 谷歌云在企业级云计算场景中宣布，在其平台上正式上线OpenAI系列模型，与原有的自家Gemini以及Anthropic的Claude形成“三足鼎立”之势。此举旨在打破大模型阵营壁垒，满足企业客户在一站式平台调度不同顶尖AI的强劲需求，使其成为首家集齐三大主流大模型的主流云厂商。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Google Cloud has integrated OpenAI models alongside Gemini and Claude into its enterprise platform, becoming the first major cloud provider to offer all three top-tier AI families in one place to meet diverse enterprise demands.

面向企业客户提供私有预览
旨在打破阵营壁垒垄断云端调度
key_points_en: Google Cloud aggregates top-3 AI models
Private preview launched for enterprise clients
Aims to break model silos and capture cloud traffic
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 大模型军备战打成了“全家桶大乱炖”，谷歌云这是主打一个“不管你粉哪家AI，终究都得给我交云费”。什么叫格局？这就是把死敌请进自家客厅还能顺便收个全屋物业费的资本艺术。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: When AI wars turn into a buffet, Google Cloud proves that you don't need to win the model race if you can just charge rent to all your rivals living under your roof.

items.title: A New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $25B in penalties after a jury found Meta misled residents about its data practices in the Cambridge Analytica scandal (Jonathan Vanian/CNBC)
items.title_en: A New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $25B in penalties after a jury found Meta misled residents about its data practices in the Cambridge Analytica scandal (Jonathan Vanian/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago.

The penalty, revealed in a court filing, comes after a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse found in September the social media giant liable for misleading state citizens about how it safeguards and collects user data and prevents harmful information from flourishing on its services.

Although the jury concluded that Meta had more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices act, with each transgression carrying a civil penalty as high as $5,000, a New Mexico judge was responsible for determining the ultimate fine. The Wednesday filing showed that the state was awarded $219.5 billion, but the penalty was ultimately reduced to $25 billion.

"The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook's repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury," New Mexico District Court Judge Francis Mathew wrote in the filing.

The judge added that interest on the penalty shall accrue at the rate of 15% each year until the fine is paid off in full.

"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," said New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez in a statement.

He added that "this penalty order demonstrates that those violations carry real consequences."

Meta chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney criticized the penalty, saying in a statement that the company is "confident" that it will "prevail on appeal."

"This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said in the statement. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online."

Meta previously resolved various Cambridge Analytica-derived data privacy lawsuits across the nation as part of an overarching August settlement of nearly $17 billion with a coalition of state attorneys general in a separate federal case related to child safety and mental health. But because New Mexico was not part of the settlement, the state's data privacy case that arose from Meta's Cambridge Analytica scandal proceeded to trial in September.

In 2022, the social media giant agreed to pay $725 million to settle a class action lawsuit that also sprang from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal that kicked off in 2018. That scandal rocked the Mark Zuckerberg-led company before its official name change to Meta, and focused on allegations that the political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica improperly accessed the information of 87 million users, raising questions about Facebook's data handling practices.

Mathew said in the filing that "Facebook did not conduct the comprehensive investigation that it promised" following the Cambridge Analytica revelations.

"Pressure from senior executives to keep costs down, lack of adequate enforcement resources, inadequate investigative techniques, and a desire not to create precedent for future investigations," all contributed to what the judge characterized as a "willfully ineffective" internal examination by Facebook, the filing said.

Former New Mexico Attorney General Hector Balderas originally filed the state's Cambridge Analytica-related lawsuit in 2021, while current AG Torrez oversaw the related trial.

Torrez also led his state's child safety-related trial against Meta that resulted in a March jury ruling that the social media company should pay $375 million for violating the state's unfair practices act. A New Mexico judge would later order Meta to pay $567 million into an abatement fund as part of a second phase of the case that determined the social media firm's actions created a public nuisance.

Meta said it disagreed with that New Mexico ruling and planned to appeal.

Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago.

The penalty, revealed in a court filing, comes after a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse found in September the social media giant liable for misleading state citizens about how it safeguards and collects user data and prevents harmful information from flourishing on its services.

A hacker group called CyberCartel used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on 400+ Latin American banks.

Not one attack
items.title_en:
A hacker group called CyberCartel used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on 400+ Latin American banks.

Not one attack. Not ten. Four hundred.

All using AI agents running in parallel.

Data stolen. Accounts accessed. Money moved.

Little human input required.

Straiker investigated. Found Claude Code session histories sitting in open directories.

Found the attacker asking Claude where to sell stolen data.

How did they get around the safety guardrails.

They told Claude they were in internal tests.

Claude believed them.

When Claude refused anyway. They switched to Grok.

Grok didn't refuse.

When Grok had limits. They switched to Kimi.

When Kimi had limits. They fell back to traditional malware.

Chain multiple models together. Each one picks up where the last one hesitated.

None of them know the full picture.

Claude thinks it's helping with testing.

Grok thinks it's just fixing code.

Kimi thinks it's just answering questions.

Together they broke into 400 banks.

The Information broke the story on October 20.

CrowdStrike confirmed it October 21.

Bank accounts in South Korea got hit the same way.

ARTEX. DeepSeek. Claude Code. All chained.

Over 68,000 people affected.

Financial Services Commission investigating.

This isn't theoretical anymore.

Not a lab demonstration. Not a proof of concept.

Real attacks. Real banks. Real money.

Automated by AI.

The moment we all waited for arrived quietly.

No announcement. No warning. Just a report.

And suddenly every AI lab is scrambling to figure out why their models are good at breaking into banks.

items.content_snippet:
16.6 MB RAM vs. 70 KB. 🤯

1,000 databases. ONE PGX process. 🐘

One idle PostgreSQL server: 16.6 MB. 
VS
One idle PGX database: just 70 KB!!

Measured on a 4 vCPU / 8 GB VM:

⚡ 128–155 MB RAM - 1,000 untouched DBs 
⚡ 213 MB - all queried once 
⚡ 283 MB - 100 active databases 
⚡ 0.33–0.43% of one CPU core at idle

This is why we built PGX. 🐘

Every AI agent deserves its own database. Not its own server.

https://t.co/Su2Mkl6ijb

items.title_en:
Holy sh*t, I just turned my TV into Jarvis with Opus 5.5 + ChatGPT voice mode

I reverse-engineered my Samsung TV with Opus 5.5...

1 sentence out loud = 6 Claude Code agents opening on my living room TV. 

here's the full guide step by step:

step 1 → put your Samsung Smart TV and your laptop on the same Wi-Fi

step 2 → paste the prompt below into Claude Code on Opus 5.5 with a photo of Settings → Support → About This TV

step 3 → Opus maps how the TV takes orders and finds the loophole: 

Samsung's own remote-control API on your home network can open any web page in the TV browser

step 4 → it spins up 6 Claude Code agents in a tmux grid on the laptop and streams them as a private page on your Wi-Fi only

step 5 → it builds a tiny "Jarvis" connector with one single tool: open the agent wall. 

ChatGPT voice mode is the ears, the connector is the hands

step 6 → press Allow on the TV once, the last time you touch the remote

step 7 → say "Open Claude Code CLI on my TV" and watch the windows pop in one by one

the result: the laptop does the work, the TV is the control room...

p.s: works on most Samsung Smart TVs with Tizen. 

mine in the video runs Smart Hub. The remote now lives in a drawer

Find full prompt below

Then read the article below on how to reverse-engineer anything
