    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.0040206750854849815,
    "guess": 77245,
    "confidence": 0.776249383996532,
    "value": 77245
   },
   "purchased_at": {
    "type": "datetime",
    "p_null": 4.136094133855295e-08,
    "guess": "2026-07-01T13:34:00",
    "confidence": 0.831464227002992,
    "value": "2026-07-01T13:34:00"
   },
   "quantity": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 5.2313655629632194e-08,
    "guess": 2,
    "confidence": 0.9997007500403496,
    "value": 2
   },
   "unit_price": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.001599092734977603,
    "guess": 7.99,
    "confidence": 0.9991279019989127,
    "value": 7.99
   },
   "subtotal": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 9.69956488461321e-08,
    "guess": 15.98,
    "confidence": 0.9999881983893096,
    "value": 15.98
   },
   "sales_tax": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 2.5511653802823275e-06,
    "guess": 0,
    "confidence": 0.9999800924450729,
    "value": 0
   },
   "tip": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 5.953857908025384e-05,
    "guess": 2.39,
    "confidence": 0.9335768781214697,
    "value": 2.39
   },
   "discount": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.9994148015975952,
    "guess": 0,
    "confidence": 0.91852733929319,
    "value": null
   }
  }
}As you can see, it was able to extract all the values from the images, alongside a confidence score. It also correctly stated that there was no discount shown in the receipt, giving the value as null.

Some values aren't in the input at all, but the input carries evidence for them. For example, values might not be in plain text but can be discerned from values around it. If you ask an LLM for an estimation, you usually get a single number with no sense of how sure the model is. It will make safe guesses or hallucinate, or reason its way around the answer. If you land on an estimate, any downstream processing can't tell a confident $180 from an unconfident $180, so it can't help you decide what is appropriate to automate in the circumstances. It is also a lot slower and more expensive to do reasoning through LLMs.

A decision model can approximate an estimate by choosing among buckets ("under $100", "$100–500", …), but buckets are coarse, every bucket adds input tokens, and each new category adds more sources of confusion for the model during its decision making process.

Clairic returns a distribution over the range you declare: a point value, a median, an 80% interval, and every percentile on request. The estimate is designed to fall inside your bounds, so there's nothing to clamp or round afterward. The width of the interval reflects data confidence: a narrow range signals high certainty, while a wide range indicates low certainty, information you can use to route another check.

    "guess": "$52.10",
    "confidence": 0.416016,
    "value": null
  }
}A few things to notice:

Here’s a real-life photo of a receipt — the text is not perfect and the angle of the image doesn’t help its legibility. We passed this image to Clairic to see what it could extract:

{
  "model": "clairic",
  "answers": {
   "order_number": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.0040206750854849815,
    "guess": 77245,
    "confidence": 0.776249383996532,
    "value": 77245
   },
   "purchased_at": {
    "type": "datetime",
    "p_null": 4.136094133855295e-08,
    "guess": "2026-07-01T13:34:00",
    "confidence": 0.831464227002992,
    "value": "2026-07-01T13:34:00"
   },
   "quantity": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 5.2313655629632194e-08,
    "guess": 2,
    "confidence": 0.9997007500403496,
    "value": 2
   },
   "unit_price": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.001599092734977603,
    "guess": 7.99,
    "confidence": 0.9991279019989127,
    "value": 7.99
   },
   "subtotal": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 9.69956488461321e-08,
    "guess": 15.98,
    "confidence": 0.9999881983893096,
    "value": 15.98
   },
   "sales_tax": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 2.5511653802823275e-06,
    "guess": 0,
    "confidence": 0.9999800924450729,
    "value": 0
   },
   "tip": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 5.953857908025384e-05,
    "guess": 2.39,
    "confidence": 0.9335768781214697,
    "value": 2.39
   },
   "discount": {
    "type": "number",
    "p_null": 0.9994148015975952,
    "guess": 0,
    "confidence": 0.91852733929319,
    "value": null
   }
  }
}As you can see, it was able to extract all the values from the images, alongside a confidence score. It also correctly stated that there was no discount shown in the receipt, giving the value as null.

Some values aren't in the input at all, but the input carries evidence for them. For example, values might not be in plain text but can be discerned from values around it. If you ask an LLM for an estimation, you usually get a single number with no sense of how sure the model is. It will make safe guesses or hallucinate, or reason its way around the answer. If you land on an estimate, any downstream processing can't tell a confident $180 from an unconfident $180, so it can't help you decide what is appropriate to automate in the circumstances. It is also a lot slower and more expensive to do reasoning through LLMs.

A decision model can approximate an estimate by choosing among buckets ("under $100", "$100–500", …), but buckets are coarse, every bucket adds input tokens, and each new category adds more sources of confusion for the model during its decision making process.

Clairic returns a distribution over the range you declare: a point value, a median, an 80% interval, and every percentile on request. The estimate is designed to fall inside your bounds, so there's nothing to clamp or round afterward. The width of the interval reflects data confidence: a narrow range signals high certainty, while a wide range indicates low certainty, information you can use to route another check.

Today, we're announcing a preview of a new class of System One-style models: extraction models. Our first one, Clairic, is available hosted on Workers AI as @cf/cloudflare/clairic.We intend to release the model open-weights soon. Clairic is an extraction model that is able to extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs — all at a significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and cheaper cost than traditional LLMs.

items.summary_en: Cloudflare unveiled Clairic, a specialized 'System One' extraction model hosted on Workers AI designed to extract, compute, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. The company claims it delivers superior accuracy, lower latency, and drastically lower costs compared to traditional LLMs, with plans to open-source model weights soon.
items.title_zh: Cloudflare发布信息抽取模型，主打超轻量反向卷大模型
items.summary_zh: Cloudflare上线抽取模型Clairic，号称以快得多的延迟与极低成本打败传统LLM进行非结构化处理

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 网络基础设施巨头Cloudflare在边缘计算平台上推出了全新提取模型Clairic，定位于专注于直觉与极速响应的‘快思考’类别模型。该模型针对非结构化数据的提取、计算与数值预测进行了专门优化，官方称其在准确度、延迟以及推断成本上均显著优于传统通用大语言模型，并计划近期开源权重。此举旨在打破业内盲目调用千亿参数模型处理简单信息抽取的算力浪费现象。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Cloudflare unveiled Clairic, a specialized 'System One' extraction model hosted on Workers AI designed to extract, compute, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. The company claims it delivers superior accuracy, lower latency, and drastically lower costs compared to traditional LLMs, with plans to open-source model weights soon.

elements_zh.what: 发布新一代针对非结构化数据的信息抽取模型Clairic，并将开源模型权重

elements_en.what: Introduced Clairic, a high-efficiency extraction model, with open-weights releasing soon
elements_en.why: Targeting the compute overkill and prohibitive costs of deploying massive LLMs for basic extraction

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 用几千亿参数的LLM从发票里提取一个总金额，就跟开航母去捕虾一样荒诞。Cloudflare终于戳破了这个皇帝的新衣：大部分企业要的不是大模型吟诗作赋，而是又快又便宜地填好Excel表格。打着卡尼曼‘快思考’理论旗号做专有小模型，既包装了高级概念，又精准收割了被GPU账单逼疯的码农。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Using a trillion-parameter LLM to scrape dates off PDF invoices is like using an aircraft carrier for shrimp fishing. Cloudflare rightly calls out the industry's ridiculous overkill: businesses don't need digital Shakespeare; they need fast, cheap parsers that fill out spreadsheets without incinerating cash.

Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.

These languages power software that banks, governments, and businesses depend on. Progress here means understanding decades of business logic and helping developers modernize those systems while preserving what works.

We’re building these capabilities around the challenges developers and enterprise customers bring us. If your team is working on these systems, tell us which languages and workflows we should tackle next.

items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Leah Nylen / Bloomberg:
The US FTC clears Publicis' $2.2B LiveRamp acquisition, subject to a consent decree requiring equal access to LiveRamp's data connectivity tools for all clients  —  The US Federal Trade Commission said it will allow Publicis Groupe SA to co
items.content_snippet: The US Federal Trade Commission said it will allow Publicis Groupe SA to complete the $2.2 billion acquisition of LiveRamp Holdings Inc …
items.summary_en: The US FTC cleared Publicis Groupe's $2.2 billion acquisition of data-connectivity platform LiveRamp, conditioned upon a consent decree. The settlement mandates that Publicis guarantee equal, non-discriminatory access to LiveRamp's essential data tools for all competing agencies and advertisers.
items.title_zh: 美监管放行阳狮22亿美元收购案，但须开放数据互联接口
items.summary_zh: 美国FTC有条件批准阳狮集团22亿美元收购数据连接巨头LiveRamp，要求确保各方平权接入

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会通过了一项附带限制条款的和解令，正式批准全球广告巨头阳狮集团以22亿美元收购数据连接服务商LiveRamp的交易。作为反垄断放行的核心交换条件，协议强制要求合并后的实体必须为所有客户及竞品广告商提供平等、无歧视的LiveRamp核心数据连接工具访问权限。监管机构此举意在防止跨国代理集团借机垄断数字营销生态链的关键身份识别与隐私数据管道。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The US FTC cleared Publicis Groupe's $2.2 billion acquisition of data-connectivity platform LiveRamp, conditioned upon a consent decree. The settlement mandates that Publicis guarantee equal, non-discriminatory access to LiveRamp's essential data tools for all competing agencies and advertisers.

elements_zh.who: 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）与阳狮集团
elements_zh.where: 美国华盛顿监管审查体系
elements_zh.what: 有条件放行22亿美元的LiveRamp并购案，并强制签订平权数据访问协议
elements_zh.why: 防止头部跨国广告巨头通过把控关键第三方底层数据连接工具实施垄断封锁

elements_en.what: Conditionally cleared the $2.2B acquisition of LiveRamp subject to a strict consent decree
elements_en.why: Preventing an ad agency monolith from weaponizing critical data infrastructure against market competitors

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 阳狮砸了22亿美刀以为能搞个独家数据护城河，结果监管机构直接在门上装了个‘公共通道’指示牌。花真金白银给全行业买单当‘基础设施代管员’，广告界的老钱们为了补齐第一方数据短板，真是打落牙齿和血吞。不过能通过审查总比被勒令拆散好，至少数据底层的抽水机握在自己手里了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Publicis shelled out $2.2 billion hoping to erect a private data moat, only for the FTC to turn it into a public utility hallway. Spending billions to become the babysitter of industry infrastructure is a bitter pill, but hey, at least they got to keep the tollbooth.

items.title_zh: 算力吞电激增，美国传统化石能源基础设施强劲回流
items.summary_zh: AI数据中心引发电力需求激增，叠加政策倾斜，美国化石能源基建出现十年最大规模逆势反扑

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 智库与环保组织披露的最新评估报告显示，美国化石能源基础设施建设正迎来过去十年间的最高峰，而可再生能源增长则显著放缓。这一转折的主要推力来自人工智能数据中心爆炸式增长、先进制程制造业回归及电网负荷见顶，迫使电网运营方退回高碳基荷能源以维持稳定供电，同时叠加了新一届政府对传统油气项目的政策倾斜。AI产业的电力饥渴正在重塑全美的能源地理格局。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A new energy report highlights a resurgence in US fossil fuel infrastructure, reaching decade-high expansion levels while renewable deployment slows down. The pivot is fueled by surging electricity consumption from AI data centers, industrial onshoring, and shifts in federal regulatory policy favoring conventional natural gas over wind and solar.

elements_zh.who: 美国电网、数据中心巨头及化石能源建设商
elements_zh.where: 美国各区域电网与大型AI算力园区
elements_zh.what: 化石能源（天然气等）设施大规模扩建，清洁能源替代进程因现实用电缺口而放缓
elements_zh.why: AI大模型训练推理引发用电激增，加上新政府政策支持，清洁能源无法短时间支撑全天候基荷

elements_en.who: US grid operators, AI hyperscalers, and fossil fuel providers
elements_en.where: Across US electrical grids and AI computing hubs
elements_en.what: Fossil fuel pipeline and plant builds hit a 10-year high as green energy expansion stalls
elements_en.why: Exploding data center power demands require reliable baseloads that intermittent renewables cannot currently guarantee

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 硅谷巨头们PPT里的‘2030净零碳排放’承诺，在遇到英伟达显卡的那一瞬间就变成了易碎品。AI训练到半夜可容不得太阳下山或者风力停摆，面对算力霸权的催促，大家心照不宣地重新点燃了天然气。拯救地球的未来宏愿，终究还是干不过下个季度财报里的大模型军备竞赛。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Big Tech’s glossy '2030 Net Zero' slide decks immediately vanished into thin air the moment Nvidia chips demanded ungodly megawatts. When training massive clusters, you can't tell GPUs to take a break because the sun set or the wind stopped blowing. Turns out the existential drive to dominate AI will gladly burn through a few dinosaurs first.

items.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
items.title_en: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition - when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they'd get from government bonds. Last Tuesady Chamath "SPAC King" Palihapitiya noticed the distressed debt, and also asked whether the AI buildout was a private credit bubble. Its shares are down more than 20 percent since Tuesday's close, which is kind of a lot! There even seemed to be some collateral damage in the market on other AI companies, too.

items.title_zh: 算力云巨头债务逼近违约级，引发全行业泡沫恐慌
items.summary_zh: CoreWeave债券收益率暴涨超千个基点跌入困境资产区，高杠杆风险拖累整个AI板块震荡

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 头部AI算力云基础设施商CoreWeave发行的债券利差上周飙升超过1000个基点，按照金融市场通用定义已正式跌入困境债务区间。华尔街知名投资人相继发声警告AI算力建设背后暗藏的巨额私募信贷泡沫，导致CoreWeave股价周跌幅超过20%，并迅速波及整个AI概念股产业链。事件起因在于该公司此前凭借英伟达GPU做高杠杆抵押借款进行激进算力扩张，其现金流造血速度正面临严峻的市场拷问。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Bonds issued by AI cloud infrastructure unicorn CoreWeave plummeted into distressed territory as yield spreads widened over 1,000 basis points. Market fears surrounding private credit exposure to hyper-leveraged GPU deployments triggered a 20%+ share slump, triggering broader contagion concerns across the AI hardware sector.

elements_zh.who: 算力独角兽CoreWeave与华尔街信贷市场
elements_zh.where: 美国高收益债券及二级资本市场
elements_zh.what: 债券跌入违约风险极高的困境资产区间，股票暴跌超20%并拖累AI板块
elements_zh.why: 过度依赖高息私募信贷抵押采购显卡，在AI应用端商业变现不及预期时遭遇债务压力

elements_en.who: CoreWeave and Wall Street private credit debt markets
elements_en.where: US high-yield bond and equities markets
elements_en.what: Bond yields touched distressed debt thresholds, cratering equity value by over 20%
elements_en.why: Heavy reliance on aggressive debt financing to buy depreciating GPUs sparks liquidity panic when end-user returns slow

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 用还没焐热的显卡做抵押，借天价高利贷去抢下一批显卡，这种左脚踩右脚上天的‘庞氏飞轮’终于卡壳了。当债券市场开始把AI算力当垃圾债折价甩卖时，说明华尔街的算盘打明白了：显卡会年年贬值，但银行的利息可一分都不会少。CoreWeave这一摔，不知道要惊醒多少还在做千亿云服务美梦的PPT吹鼓手。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Collateralizing today’s GPUs to take out high-yield debt to buy tomorrow’s GPUs was an ingenious flywheel right up until basic math caught up. When bonds slip into distressed territory, it means credit markets realized hardware depreciates fast while debt compounding never sleeps. This cold shower reminds everyone that AI datacenters aren't magical money printers.

items.summary_en: Robotics foundation model startup Dream Labs secured a massive $90 million seed round led by B Capital and Kindred Ventures. The company is developing Dream-1, a robotics foundation model trained directly on human demonstration videos, providing API access for diverse physical hardware platforms.
items.title_zh: 机器人基座初创公司完成九千万美元巨额种子轮
items.summary_zh: Dream Labs凭人类视频训练的机器人基础模型获9000万美元融资，将向外界开放API

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 具身智能初创企业Dream Labs宣布完成规模达9000万美元的种子轮融资，由顶级风投机构联合领投。该团队推出了名为Dream-1的机器人通用基础模型，其技术路径核心在于纯粹通过吸收人类操作日常行为的视频数据进行预训练，并计划将这套多模态具身能力以云端API形式向第三方硬件厂商开放。本轮融资充分证明资本市场正从大语言模型转向抢跑具身物理AI控制大脑。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Robotics foundation model startup Dream Labs secured a massive $90 million seed round led by B Capital and Kindred Ventures. The company is developing Dream-1, a robotics foundation model trained directly on human demonstration videos, providing API access for diverse physical hardware platforms.

elements_zh.who: 机器人技术初创公司Dream Labs及联合领投风投
elements_zh.where: 硅谷具身智能创投圈
elements_zh.what: 完成9000万美元巨型种子轮融资，推出基于人类视频预训练的Dream-1模型与API
elements_zh.why: 利用低成本人类动作视频绕过实体机器人遥操作数据匮乏的瓶颈，加速具身智能软件落地

elements_en.who: Embodied AI startup Dream Labs, backed by B Capital and Kindred Ventures
elements_en.what: Secured a $90M seed funding round and unveiled its video-trained Dream-1 model API
elements_en.why: Solving the physical data bottleneck in robotics by learning physical dynamics directly from passive human video

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 现在连‘种子轮’的起跑线都已经卷到9000万美元了，普通创业者看了只能抹眼泪。看人类做家务视频就能让机器人在现实里搬砖？这饼画得确实够性感。不过等硬件厂商真接上API才发现，屏幕里丝滑的动作落到机械臂上，往往逃不过把咖啡洒满一地的宿命。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When a 'seed round' hits $90 million, it's safe to say words have lost all meaning in venture land. Training robots to manipulate reality just by watching YouTube sounds brilliant in pitch decks, but between video pixels and a jerky robotic claw crushing coffee cups, there lies a painful engineering chasm.

items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Paige Smith / Bloomberg:
Ramp says it applied to the US OCC for a trust bank charter that, if approved, would allow it to offer fiduciary investment management and digital asset custody  —  Financial technology firm Ramp said it applied with the Office of the Comp
items.content_snippet: Financial technology firm Ramp said it applied with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a trust bank charter …
items.summary_en: Fintech unicorn Ramp filed an application with the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) for a national trust bank charter. If granted, the charter would empower Ramp to offer fiduciary investment management services and custody digital assets for its commercial clients.
items.title_zh: 金融科技巨头申办信托银行牌照，剑指数字资产托管
items.summary_zh: 支出管理独角兽Ramp向美监管申请信托银行牌照，获批后将可提供受托投资与数字资产托管

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知名企业财务与支出自动化管理平台Ramp已向美国货币监理署（OCC）正式递交全国性信托银行牌照申请。如果顺利获批，该牌照将赋予Ramp直接提供受托投资管理以及数字资产合规托管等高阶金融服务的能力。Ramp此举旨在从单一的账单与报销Saas工具升级为受联邦严格监管的金融全周期账户，以锁定企业客户的闲置现金管理与加密资产业务。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Fintech unicorn Ramp filed an application with the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) for a national trust bank charter. If granted, the charter would empower Ramp to offer fiduciary investment management services and custody digital assets for its commercial clients.

elements_zh.who: 金融科技独角兽Ramp及美国货币监理署（OCC）
elements_zh.where: 美国联邦金融监管体系
elements_zh.what: 申请全国信托银行牌照，以获权从事信托资管与数字资产托管业务
elements_zh.why: 突破第三方银行合作伙伴依赖，做大资金沉淀收益并切入高客单价的企业加密金库

elements_en.who: Fintech unicorn Ramp and US OCC regulators
elements_en.what: Applied for a national trust bank charter covering fiduciary services and crypto custody
elements_en.why: Eliminating intermediary banking friction to capture corporate treasury yields and enterprise digital asset management

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 所有发企业信用卡的软件公司，终极梦想都是把手伸进客户的钱包底盘当银行家。给企业管发票只能赚点过路费，要是能把客户的闲钱乃至比特币名正言顺地锁在自己的托管池里，那才叫旱涝保收。披着极简软件外皮的SaaS新贵，最后活成了它当年扬言要颠覆的华尔街老银行。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Every corporate expense management SaaS eventually realizes that parsing receipts is chump change compared to actually being a bank. If you can legally sit on enterprise treasuries and custody their crypto, you've hit peak fintech. They spent years mocking traditional banks, only to realize the endgame is literally becoming one.

items.title: Sources: Nscale is in talks for a second deal with Anthropic worth ~$45B to deliver 460MW of computing power at its West Virginia campus using Vera Rubin chips (Bloomberg)
items.title_en: Sources: Nscale is in talks for a second deal with Anthropic worth ~$45B to deliver 460MW of computing power at its West Virginia campus using Vera Rubin chips (Bloomberg)
items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Bloomberg:
Sources: Nscale is in talks for a second deal with Anthropic worth ~$45B to deliver 460MW of computing power at its West Virginia campus using Vera Rubin chips  —  Nscale Ltd., the AI cloud computing firm, is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropi
items.content_snippet: Nscale Ltd., the AI cloud computing firm, is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic PBC in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion …
items.summary_en: Emerging AI cloud firm Nscale is negotiating a landmark computing power contract with Anthropic valued at approximately $45 billion. The proposed agreement calls for Nscale to provide 460 megawatts of high-density capacity utilizing next-generation Vera Rubin chips from its West Virginia datacenter campus.
items.title_zh: 算力服务商或获四百五十亿美元大单，向大模型厂供电
items.summary_zh: 算力基础设施商Nscale正与Anthropic洽谈450亿美元大单，提供460兆瓦下一代算力

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 新兴AI云算力服务商Nscale目前正与大模型独角兽Anthropic深入洽谈一笔价值高达约450亿美元的算力采购补充协议。按照拟议条款，Nscale将在其位于西弗吉尼亚州的数据中心园区，基于下一代先进芯片架构向Anthropic稳定交付高达460兆瓦（MW）的超高密度计算基础设施。这一天文数字级的交易凸显了顶级模型厂商在训练下一代前沿多模态大模型时对长周期算力与能源的饥渴争夺。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Emerging AI cloud firm Nscale is negotiating a landmark computing power contract with Anthropic valued at approximately $45 billion. The proposed agreement calls for Nscale to provide 460 megawatts of high-density capacity utilizing next-generation Vera Rubin chips from its West Virginia datacenter campus.

elements_zh.who: 算力基础设施云服务商Nscale与Anthropic
elements_zh.where: 美国西弗吉尼亚州超大型算力中心
elements_zh.what: 磋商一项约450亿美元的巨型协议，锁定460兆瓦的下一代算力容量
elements_zh.why: 大模型厂商必须提前数年抢占超万卡集群所需的电力接入与未来一代硬件产能

elements_en.who: AI cloud infrastructure provider Nscale and Anthropic
elements_en.what: In talks for a ~$45B contract to deliver 460MW of computing infrastructure with Vera Rubin chips
elements_en.why: Hyperscalers need to lock down massive power reserves and future-gen silicon allocations years ahead

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 张嘴就是450亿美金加460兆瓦电力，这胃口哪是在训练算法，分明是在修赛博三峡大坝。连芯片都直接锁定到未来的鲁宾架构，说明顶级玩家已经彻底接受了现实：搞AGI不是比谁代码写得漂亮，就是纯粹的‘烧钱堆电量’。只要VC和云厂商敢掏钱，这帮AI巨头就能把整个州的电网全部买空。
ai_analysis.insight_en: A casual $45 billion for 460 megawatts—Anthropic isn't training algorithms; they're attempting to power a small sovereign nation with pure silicon. Locking down unreleased Rubin chips years in advance proves AGI development is less about poetic software and more about who can scorch through an entire state's electrical grid the fastest.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 新兴AI云算力服务商Nscale目前正与大模型独角兽Anthropic深入洽谈一笔价值高达约450亿美元的算力采购补充协议。按照拟议条款，Nscale将在其位于西弗吉尼亚州的数据中心园区，基于下一代先进芯片架构向Anthropic稳定交付高达460兆瓦（MW）的超高密度计算基础设施。这一天文数字级的交易凸显了顶级模型厂商在训练下一代前沿多模态大模型时对长周期算力与能源的饥渴争夺。

The proposed agreement calls for Nscale to provide 460 megawatts of high-density capacity utilizing next-generation Vera Rubin chips from its West Virginia datacenter campus.
key_points_zh: 洽谈450亿美元史诗级订单：Nscale与Anthropic第二轮算力深绑
规模达460兆瓦超大电荷：基于西弗吉尼亚园区及下一代架构算力
算力争夺终局化：大模型寡头竞争彻底演化为电网与万卡硬件锁死战

items.title: OpenAI Engineer Accused of Spying on Executives Ordered to Remain in Custody
items.title_en: OpenAI Engineer Accused of Spying on Executives Ordered to Remain in Custody
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
US prosecutors alleged Abdulrahman Alfozan is a flight risk because the Saudi Arabian government has offered to support him with no strings attached. They cited, for example, the Saudi consulate’s offer to work with a bail bonds firm to help fund Alfozan’s release.

Federal magistrate judge Alex Tse questioned whether Alfozan is an “asset” for the kingdom and how a bond backed by the government could keep him in the country. “I find that problematic,” Tse said. “It seems like a blank check. ‘We’re going to pay whatever the court wants to get him out.’ I’m more interested in people from his family wanting to put up assets.”

William Pernik, an attorney for Alfozan, dismissed the flight risk worries as baseless. But he failed to convince the judge that Alfozan was committed to his life in the US. “There is a real threat here that once he leaves the case is over,” Tse said.

Aflozan appeared in an orange prison uniform and a medical face mask pulled down over his neck on Monday in Tse’s San Francisco courtroom, which was filled to capacity with journalists, students on a field trip, and about 20 people supporting Alfozan.

Employee attempts to steal confidential company information are common in Silicon Valley. But Alfozan’s case has drawn international attention for the alleged amateur spycraft and geopolitical tensions at the center of it. Authorities haven’t offered a potential motive, but have noted Alfozan has worked for a Saudi venture capital firm, offered consulting services to Saudi companies, and is supposedly friendly with people high up in the Saudi government.

Pernik said there was no evidence of Alfozan spying for Saudi Arabia or engaging in something covert. “It’s not as if he sneaked in under the covers of darkness,” he said of the OpenAI conference room. “This was an open room where anybody could work in.”

After the hour-long hearing, Pernik told reporters he was disappointed with the custody ruling and would continue to try to fight it.

While Alfozan is a US permanent resident who had been on the path to obtaining citizenship, his ties to his native Saudi Arabia have come under scrutiny. Prosecutors allege that Alfozan was “in frequent communications via WhatsApp” with a member of the Saudi royal family throughout 2025 and 2026.

The Saudi royal, who is not identified, was allegedly recruiting Alfozan to return to the country for a job working on a forthcoming AI initiative, according to a court filing. “Saudi needs you more then [sic] the US!” the individual wrote to Alfozan this past May, per the filing. Alfozan allegedly “responded ‘100,’ indicating he agreed.”

US authorities also allege that the Saudi government bought Alfozan's wife and infant son a ticket to return to the country a few days after his arrest. She ended up leaving sooner on another flight booked by her sister’s husband, who works for the Saudi navy, according to attorneys for both sides.

Alfozan's wife has not been accused of wrongdoing and the FBI last week declined to comment on whether she would face any charges.

Alfozan was at OpenAI for just over a year when the AI lab discovered a covert audio recording device hidden in a wad of toilet paper behind a TV in an executive conference room used for confidential business meetings. OpenAI found the device in late September, connected it to Alfozan, and then fired him earlier this month just before the FBI arrested him.

Alfozan faces five years in prison on a single count of using a device to intercept communications, but prosecutors say additional charges are possible. Included among the government’s evidence are alleged conversations between Alfozan and an AI chatbot in which he asked for help setting up listening devices. Prosecutors also produced a photo taken of Alfozan looking behind the TV after OpenAI had removed the recorder. It’s unclear what, if anything, was recorded because the device’s data was encrypted, according to authorities.

Authorities say they also found components for recording devices at Alfozan’s home and photos of other OpenAI monitors and another OpenAI conference room on his phone. OpenAI previously said it recovered a second listening device in a bag Alfozan brought to the office and left unattended.

Pernik claimed the electronics at Alfozan’s home were for home monitoring projects, including trying to improve a smart litter box for their cat. “This is a gentleman who spent 15 years of life immersed at this intersection of technology and personal life,” Pernik told the judge.

Authorities said ahead of the hearing that they believed Alfozan had the means to flee. They cited the $385,000 salary and $2.2 million profit-sharing package he received while working at OpenAI as well as other funds he earned from previous gigs at Meta and other US tech companies.

According to Alfozan's attorneys, his wife needed to leave the US to renew her American student visa. Alfozan had planned to accompany her on the trip before being arrested. They had a one-way ticket to Riyadh, which Alfozan’s attorneys said was typical for him because he sometimes had to return earlier than planned for work.

According to Alfozan's attorneys, his wife needed to leave the US to renew her American student visa. Alfozan had planned to accompany her on the trip before being arrested. They had a one-way ticket to Riyadh, which Alfozan’s attorneys said was typical for him because he sometimes had to return earlier than planned for work.

Nas Yasin, another attorney for Alfozan, said his wife’s flight was booked by her sister’s husband in his personal capacity. Yasin added that Alfozan’s wife had just secured a visitor visa from the US and planned to return to California from Saudi Arabia as soon as Tuesday. Alfozan’s next court date is scheduled for November 6.

items.summary_en: A federal magistrate judge in San Francisco ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan to remain in custody on corporate espionage charges, citing immense flight risks. Prosecutors revealed that the Saudi Arabian government offered unconditional financial backing to fund his bail, which the judge deemed equivalent to a blank check. items.title_zh: OpenAI涉间谍前员工被拒保释
items.summary_zh: 一名涉嫌刺探高管机密的OpenAI工程师在旧金山联邦法庭被裁定继续羁押，法官认定沙特领馆主动全额包揽保释金构成极大潜逃风险
items.article_content_zh:
根据旧金山联邦法院庭审实录，涉案被告阿卜杜勒拉赫曼·阿尔福赞身着橙色囚服出庭。检方出具的指控证据显示，其在任职期间涉嫌利用特权系统刺探并窃取公司高管层的内部敏感机密。在保释辩论环节，沙特驻旧金山领事馆明确表示愿同保释金经纪公司合作，全额兜底阿尔福赞获释所需的任何担保款项，这一罕见举动随即遭到检方与主审法官的严厉质疑。

联邦治安法官亚历克斯·谢在法庭上直言，主权国家政府无上限开具资金担保的行为极不寻常，这本质上属于潜逃的空白支票，一旦当事人离境返回沙特，美方司法管辖权将直接失效。尽管辩护律师极力主张被告具有定居美国的真实意愿，法官仍判定其人身潜逃隐患无法通过常规财务约束排除，最终签署命令继续羁押。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在旧金山联邦地区法院举行的保释听证会上，法官正式裁定涉嫌非法窃取高管敏感信息的OpenAI工程师阿卜杜勒拉赫曼·阿尔福赞不得保释、继续羁押。检方指控沙特领事馆主动提出全额垫付保释金以协助其出狱，法官认为这种无附加条件的政府背书形同潜逃空头支票，一旦离境案件将彻底终结。该案源于大厂核心机密与地缘政治利益交织，其非法外泄敏感资料的行为直接触犯了联邦刑事法律。

The ruling stems from allegations that Alfozan illicitly accessed and stole confidential internal data from OpenAI executives.

give Claude Code 15 motion design styles, then ask it to turn them into a studio that never stops rendering

how to set it up:

> pick a style and give Claude Code a motion reference: a clip, a gif or a few frames

> one prompt = one 10s film, visuals and sound all from code
> repeat for all 15 styles and save every prompt as a reusable preset
> put them on one loop: every style gets a live tile, a preview and a copy button

now you don't start from a blank timeline. you pick a style, copy the prompt, swap the title, render

items.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
items.title_en: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Recently fixed vulnerabilities in the Plex Media Server are under active exploitation in attacks that, when successful, install malware, including cryptominers and residential proxy apps, a researcher said.

Plex fixed four vulnerabilities at the start of last month. Three weeks later, published CVE designations revealed five vulnerabilities, with one of them carrying a severity rating of 8.6 out of 10. A researcher last week revealed an exploit that chained four of them together to achieve remote code execution of the device running a vulnerable Plex version. The researcher named the chain "Plex2Shell."

The new details allowed a separate researcher to create a honeypot that could track attempts in the wild to exploit the vulnerability chain. Within a day, the researcher began seeing active scanning of the simulated Plex server and eventually successful attempts to infect devices. So far, successful attacks are installing two payloads. One is a cryptominer, which uses the device to mine cryptocurrency and deposit it into a wallet controlled by the attacker. The other payload is residential proxy software, which allows people to anonymize their Internet activity (much of it illegal

Cybersecurity researchers disclosed a four-vulnerability exploit chain, dubbed 'Plex2Shell', allowing remote code execution with a severity rating of 8.6 out of 10. items.title_zh: 知名媒体服务器曝高危漏洞遭黑客利用
items.summary_zh: 知名家庭流媒体服务器系统被曝存在高危远程代码执行漏洞，黑客已在全网广泛扫描并植入挖矿木马与住宅代理程序
items.article_content_zh:
针对家用流媒体服务器Plex的安全威胁正在急速发酵。网络安全专家公布的分析指出，官方虽已推送修复补丁，但随后公布的技术细节导致黑客成功反编译出名为“Plex2Shell”的组合利用工具。该攻击利用了四组连续缺陷，绕过了访问控制层并在未授权的宿主系统上直接获取远程命令执行（RCE）权限，其单一缺陷严重程度评级高达8.6分。

安全人员搭建的蜜罐探针记录显示，概念验证代码公开后24小时内公网即出现了针对特定端口的密集扫描。一旦攻击者成功打入目标系统，后台会立刻被植入常驻型恶意程序：一方面榨取主机CPU资源进行加密货币挖掘，另一方面将受害者的家庭宽带转变为住宅级出口代理，用于隐匿地下黑产和网络犯罪流量。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 全球广泛使用的Plex媒体服务器近期修复的多个高危安全缺陷正在野外遭受黑客大规模自动化利用。安全专家披露，黑客通过将包含8.6级严重缺陷在内的四个漏洞进行武器化串联，已形成可在未授权状态下直接获取设备控制权的攻击链。部署在公网的蜜罐监测证实，未及时修补补丁的服务器正被黑客迅速攻陷并植入隐蔽的加密货币挖矿木马及流量代理中继。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Critical vulnerabilities in the widely used Plex Media Server are under active weaponization by threat actors in the wild. Cybersecurity researchers disclosed a four-vulnerability exploit chain, dubbed 'Plex2Shell', allowing remote code execution with a severity rating of 8.6 out of 10. Real-time honeypot monitoring confirmed that unpatched servers are being mass-compromised to deploy cryptominers and residential proxy apps.

elements_zh.where: 全球公网暴露的家用私有云及流媒体网络节点
elements_zh.what: 名为Plex2Shell的四合一漏洞攻击链遭黑客恶意扫描利用，受害者设备被批量沦陷为矿机与代理肉鸡
elements_zh.why: 旧版本服务器存在代码逻辑与鉴权严重漏洞，且大量极客用户未及时部署最新固件更新

elements_en.who: Plex development team and independent security researchers
elements_en.where: Global network edge running self-hosted Plex Media Server instances
elements_en.what: Active exploitation of 'Plex2Shell' exploit chain enabling unauthorized RCE to plant cryptominers and proxies
elements_en.why: Critical input and authentication flaws left unpatched across wide user-deployed home servers

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 许多极客辛辛苦苦攒几十块硬盘组影音库只为了躺平看片，结果自家电表倒转成了黑客的免费矿机和暗网跳板。从私人家庭影院沦落为黑客挖矿肉鸡，中间仅仅隔着一次被推迟的系统升级。老老实实去点更新吧，别让家里的NAS比你打工还要拼命在深夜里狂飙‘致富’。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Self-hosting enthusiasts spend thousands building dream media rigs only to give hackers a free cryptomining node and darknet proxy. The distance between a pristine 4K home theater and a compromised botnet zombie is just one ignored patch notification. Update your boxes, or accept that your NAS is working harder for cybercriminals than you are for your boss.

Radiology has been a prime target, with Geoff Hinton once claiming, “people should stop training radiologists now, it’s just completely obvious that within five years, deep learning is going to do better than radiologists”, which is funny since he said that in 2016. There is now more demand for radiologists than ever, so clearly things did not turn out the way many thought. Here I will make a prediction that while radiology will change in the coming decade, radiologists will not be automated away any time soon. I will use radiology as an example but I think these principles will broadly apply to any field where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence.

First of all, we have seen in the short history of language models that there is a “jagged edge of intelligence”, where AI excels at verifiable tasks with a lot of data but is underwhelming on less common tasks. One thing most AI researchers underestimate about radiology is that it is actually extremely multi-task. There are at least a hundred conditions that can be diagnosed from x-rays alone, and thousands using CT and MRI. AI will first master common and easy-to-see conditions and it will not be as good as experts at less-common diseases just because there is less data for that. This jagged edge will certainly improve over time but this means that AI will certainly be used as a triage tool at first, rather than full automation in one go. I would guess that this process from solid triage tool to full automation would take 3-5 years in the best case scenario, because training AI to get all the edge cases right will be bottlenecked by data collection of rare diseases, and also because radiology isn’t currently a focus for frontier labs.

Second, there will be elastic demand for radiology as it gets cheaper per unit. I think elastic demand (“Jevons paradox”) is the most underrated phenomenon when people think about AI automation. In software, it is obvious that I have way more demand than before because Claude Code makes it so easy. These days I ask Claude Code to build a custom three-thousand line html viewer to help me visualize every little RL run that I do. The same thing will happen in radiology. If there is essentially no cost or latency of interpreting an MRI, a physician can order many scans preemptively to better diagnose a case. So with AI tools, a radiologist might have to read only 20% of inbound scans, but there might be 5x more scans inbound. Many developing countries have fewer than one radiologist per million people and they will also want to send a lot of radiology to be interpreted.

Longer term, cheap and fast radiology interpretation will also drive incentives to build cheaper radiology scanners. If an MRI had essentially no latency for interpretation, medical devices companies will want to build much cheaper MRI machines that can be used more frequently, perhaps even in the middle of a surgery. AI will accelerate the development of scanning technology, too. If a full body MRI was only $100 dollars I would totally want to get one every month instead of every two years. I can imagine a world where people get 10 or 100x the number of scans they do today, largely for preventative care, if radiology were 10-100x cheaper.

Third, even if we did have a model that could outperform the world’s best radiologists today, that would not be the end of all work on radiology. Medicine is a field of change. We may develop new treatment protocols that require reading radiology images in a way that radiologists currently aren’t used to. New scanners may reveal diseases that we cannot currently diagnose today with radiology alone. Some radiologists will change their work from reading scans to doing frontier research to advance our understanding of radiology and translate new knowledge into updated models.

Moreover, I am sure that we will ask for more out of our AI models than ever before. With a good flywheel, we may one day train AI models that can use radiology images to predict disease probabilities far into the future. With good prediction algorithms, cancer may be detected months earlier than we can detect it now. Society will invest a lot into this research and this will contribute even more to increased demand for radiology and the best AI around it.

On top of all of this, the medical system is typically slower to adopt new technology and has more regulation compared to technology companies. There is legacy infrastructure and medical centers need to constantly support patients which makes it hard to integrate new technology. This is even more true in developing countries. Moreover data access tends to be limited due to HIPAA, deidentification, IRBs, etc. So I think radiologists will be in demand for a while.

items.title_en:
Stop building a 14th AI agent for a problem 30 people have.

People are building rocket ships to cross the street.

A better model turns your tool into a free feature in about 18 months. Maybe 24 if you're lucky.

Meanwhile the guy who posted twice a day that whole time has 15,000 people reading everything he writes.

When the next tool drops, he's the one selling it.

Unless you're shipping a true breakthrough, a mediocre product from someone with 15,000 people who trust them outsells your great one this year.

items.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
items.title_en: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NT Files System drive partition. As reported by Phoronix, the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.

Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS's stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.

However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn't be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still "lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support." So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactO

items.article_content_zh:
旨在完全复刻Windows NT架构的开源操作系统ReactOS迎来里程碑进展。根据官方技术公报，系统安装程序已全面接纳NTFS文件系统格式，终端用户无需再像以往一样将安装介质和硬盘空间强行格式化为兼容性受限的FAT32格式。这是该项目自确立全面兼容Windows Server 2003目标以来，在系统存储引导层迈出的关键一步。

NTFS文件系统最初可追溯至1993年的Windows NT 3.1时代，并在随后的几十年中成为微软生态的标准底层标准。尽管ReactOS此次成功突破了只读与受限引导的壁垒，但开发维护团队在代码说明中明确提示，当前发布的NTFS驱动程序尚未集成内存读写缓存、掉电保护日志以及Windows内建的访问控制安全描述符，其实际运行性能与系统健壮性仍处于早期试验水平。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 旨在实现Windows二进制兼容的开源操作系统项目ReactOS取得阶段性技术成果，正式实现允许用户直接将系统安装至NTFS文件系统分区。长期以来该系统受底层驱动限制只能依赖过时的FAT32分区安装，此次对现代文件系统支持的技术攻坚消除了迈向公测阶段的核心技术路障。不过团队坦言新驱动目前仍缺少缓存加速、日志恢复及安全策略机制，整体运行性能与稳定性仍待打磨。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The open-source Windows clone project ReactOS marked a key milestone by introducing native installation support onto NTFS drive partitions. Previously restricted to decades-old FAT32 partitions, this advancement removes a major hurdle on the operating system's roadmap toward reaching official beta status. Developers cautioned that the new driver currently lacks caching, journaling, and advanced security capabilities.

			POSTED ON OCTOBER 19, 2026 TO Core Infra, Data Center Engineering, Data Infrastructure, ML Applications, Networking & Traffic, Production Engineering
			Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster		

	

			
										
		
	
					
				By Kevin Lee, Yashar Bayani, Ahmed Sharif, Yee Jiun Song			
			

	
	

		
With the recent release of the Muse family of foundational models, we want to take you inside the infrastructure that has made it all possible.
The first phase of Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster, is already complete and we’re working toward scaling it to comprise  ~1 million GPUs.
Prometheus also features technologies like closed-loop liquid cooling to help it operate efficiently.

Right now, in New Albany, Ohio, Meta is undertaking its most ambitious AI infrastructure project to date. Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster, is an advancement in our infrastructure that is training the next generation of foundational models that will bring new AI experiences to billions of people.

Two years ago, New Albany was a conventional data center site running web traffic. With advancements in hardware, networking and building design, we reworked this site to be home to training programs for frontier models. We’re building the supercluster in phases. The first phase has already been completed and was used to train our Muse foundational models, including the Muse Wonder models, our new frontier models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks.

Large training jobs require everything to work optimally to sustain their performance; an issue on a single host can slow down or stop the entire job, lowering its ‘goodput’. By focusing on improving our systems’ stability and reliability we were able to achieve more than 85% goodput for pre-training runs and more than 90% goodput for reinforcement learning (RL) runs of Muse Wonder. During these training runs, we were able to achieve an overall wall-clock mean time between interruptions (MTBI) of ~47k GPU hours. Since then, we have landed further changes across our fleet including firmware fixes to increase MTBI to more than 54K GPU hours, and we are constantly improving it.

Now, we’re continuing to scale Prometheus with our next frontier models from Meta Superintelligence Labs in mind.

The Prometheus supercluster is housed in Meta’s New Albany, Ohio, data center.

Today, Prometheus comprises an array of hundreds of thousands of GPUs across multiple interconnected buildings, including traditional and AI-optimized data center buildings and rapid deployment structures, all tightly interconnected by miles of fiber and functioning as a single machine.

This capacity allows us to pursue larger models and longer context windows than were previously practical. At full scale, Prometheus will comprise roughly 1 million distributed GPUs, all functioning in lockstep.

Prometheus currently deploys two NVIDIA GPU platforms, with a third (based on NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin NVL72) arriving soon. Each represents a generational leap in performance and efficiency, leveraging our NVL72 rack architecture where 72 GPUs act as a single accelerator within the same network fabric.

Our first platform, Catalina, leverages the NVIDIA GB200 NVL72. We deploy the Ariel variant, a two-rack configuration in which 36 GPUs per rack are interconnected via NVLink to form a unified 72-GPU domain. Catalina provides improvements in raw compute and memory capacity compared to Grand Teton H100. It leverages our Open Rack V3 (ORv3) high-power rack (HPR) structure, an open hardware design contributed to the Open Compute Project (OCP).

The Ariel variant of GB200 NVL72 pairs each NVIDIA Blackwell GPU with an NVIDIA Grace CPU and 2x NVIDIA ConnectX-7 400G NICs at a 1:1 CPU-to-GPU ratio, letting us deploy 800G of I/O per GPU earlier than the rest of the industry. We chose Ariel because the GB200 NVL72 scaled up nearly every other dimension relative to the NVIDIA H100: FLOPS, HBM bandwidth, scale-up bandwidth, and scale-up domain size, while scale-out bandwidth per GPU would have stayed at 400G. We expected that imbalance to cost performance, so we opted for a configuration that delivers 800G of scale-out per GPU. This also gave us more uniformity of spec as the region expanded over time and 800G scale-out became available.

Our second platform, Clemente, moves to the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 and improves on Catalina at both the GPU and the platform level. GB300 raises HBM capacity per GPU by 1.5x, from 192 GB to 288 GB, and dense FP4 throughput by a similar factor, while roughly doubling attention (softmax) acceleration. At the platform level, scale-out is no longer the constraint it was on the GB200 NVL72: NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNICs deliver 800G per GPU natively, so the capability we deployed early on Ariel becomes the baseline. That, together with a 2:1 GPU-to-CPU ratio, allows Clemente to pack the full 72-GPU domain into a single rack, streamlining our physical deployment. Clemente can be deployed with our modular Air-Assisted Liquid Cooling (AALC) or use Facility Liquid Cooling (FLC) in our newly designed data centers. Serviceability also improves substantially, with reduced cabling.

In traditional web services, the data center network transports requests and responses between services whose instances typically don’t require high bandwidth, high performance, and tight, lock-step coordination across many servers. Large-scale AI training requires all these, meaning the network that connects them is now an important part of AI workloads. To best address this, in addition to the standard data center network connecting servers, several years ago we added a second dedicated data network based on Ethernet, called the Back-End (BE) network, to enable direct GPU-to-GPU communication both within and across data center buildings.

Large pre-training jobs partition the training into data-parallel model replicas, creating a hierarchy in network usage: Latency-sensitive and bandwidth-sensitive operations concentrate within a replica, while traffic that is more tolerant of higher latency and less bandwidth is scheduled between replicas. Our network is designed to match this hierarchy, with low-latency, high-bandwidth fabrics within buildings and an aggregation network connecting the building fabrics.

We work closely with Meta Superintelligence Labs to ensure the parallelism design, traffic patterns, and communication algorithms and software are optimized to minimize exposure of any network communication. This keeps the GPUs as busy as possible and not waiting on the network.

The Meta team has employed these networking concepts in earlier building-scale, 24K GPU clusters and our region-scale, 100K+ GPU cluster over the last several years, and we took them to a new level of scale and distance in Prometheus.

At the building level, each Ethernet-based fabric interconnects up to 20,736 GPUs through a high-bandwidth, low-latency multi-layer topology. Our initial design used a Disaggregated Scheduled Fabric (DSF) to mitigate the network congestion caused by training collectives that typically have a small number of large, long-lived network flows that collide under traditional load-balancing techniques; it does this by utilizing sub-packet-level multipath routing and packet re-ordering in the fabric along with virtual output queues and credit-based end-to-end flow control.

As Ethernet NIC technology advanced, enabling packet re-ordering at the endpoint, we were able to update to a Non-Scheduled Fabric (NSF) utilizing shallow-buffer 51.2T Ethernet switches, such as Minipack3 with Dynamic Load Balancing and the NVIDIA Spectrum-4 switch ASIC-based Minipack3N with NVIDIA’s Adaptive Routing on ConnectX NICs. Both DSF and NSF are based on Meta’s FBOSS networking stack, giving us the control to rapidly iterate on and optimize the fabrics in Prometheus, and the visibility to operate these clusters at scale.

The Backend Aggregation (BAG) network is a multi-layer hub-and-spoke network that connects building-level fabrics across the Prometheus cluster, spanning 2 km to over 100 km. It is built with Arista 7800-series chassis running deep-buffered Broadcom Jericho3 silicon, delivering multiple Pbps of bandwidth per region pair.

Running pretraining over this network required a dedicated optimization effort with Meta Superintelligence Labs to ensure training was not slowed down, especially given speed-of-light constraints at these distances.

Pulling this all together, the complexity of the Prometheus network involves millions of miles of fiber strand, tens of thousands of switches, and millions of optics — from 2×400G FR4 LITE short-reach, low-cost pluggables inside the buildings to 800G-ZR coherent optics for links beyond ~10 km.

At Prometheus’ scale, every component needs to be monitored for reliability. A single fault anywhere can halt an entire training job and waste valuable compute resources.

Maintaining reliability at this level requires a co-engineering model with NVIDIA that goes beyond a traditional vendor dynamic. Teams are deeply embedded at our data centers, sharing real-time telemetry and running joint triage sessions to decompose every system halt by its root cause.

This attribution-driven accountability model ensures both sides are focused on targeted improvements. While Meta optimizes scheduling and infrastructure, NVIDIA addresses firmware, signal diagnostics, and memory handling. This transparency eliminates ambiguity and drives faster fixes across both organizations.

The transition from the H100 generation’s NVL8 architecture to NVL72 has fundamentally redefined our approach to infrastructure resilience. In the NVL8 era, the scale-up domain — the group of GPUs tightly coupled via NVLink for tensor parallelism — was limited to eight units. With NVL72, that domain expands to 72 GPUs, increasing the fault blast radius by 9X.

The larger scale-up domain is what gives NVL72 its bandwidth advantage, but it also makes the 72-GPU rack the unit of allocation we plan capacity around. Training parallelism maps most efficiently onto power-of-two group sizes, so each NVL72 domain runs a 64-GPU slice and keeps its remaining eight GPUs as in-rack spares. When a GPU fails, a spare takes its place immediately, so the job restarts from its last checkpoint instead of waiting on hardware repair, and the rack stays in the job. The in-rack redundancy pushes the effective rack fault rate down to the floor set by failures that can remove an entire pod; for rarer whole-rack faults we hold roughly 2% additional racks in reserve. Most of that margin (11%) falls out of the 64-of-72 slice geometry rather than being an absolute reliability tax.

Physical complexity further intensifies these reliability requirements. A single NVL72 domain incorporates 5,184 tuned differential-pair signaling links operating at 200 Gbps, each traversing multiple potential points of failure, including GPU SerDes, compute tray PCBs, cable cartridges, and switch tray interfaces. Maintaining consistent signal integrity across this dense fabric — at 200 Gbps per lane — represents an unprecedented engineering challenge at this scale.

Our distributed checkpointing architecture asynchronously saves the model state — including gradients and optimizer data — to multi-tier storage. We use delta checkpointing and in-memory staging to ensure these saves happen with minimal impact on training throughput.

These two fault recovery mechanisms combine with a sparing strategy that utilizes pre-allocated spare GPU trays within a rack, as well as spare racks, to minimize the time to bring up replacement hardware and reduce the amount of work lost to hardware failures

			POSTED ON OCTOBER 19, 2026 TO Core Infra, Data Center Engineering, Data Infrastructure, ML Applications, Networking & Traffic, Production Engineering
			Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster		

	

			
										
		
	
					
				By Kevin Lee, Yashar Bayani, Ahmed Sharif, Yee Jiun Song			
			

	
	

		
With the recent release of the Muse family of foundational models, we want to take you inside the infrastructure that has made it all possible.
The first phase of Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster, is already complete and we’re working toward scaling it to comprise  ~1 million GPUs.
Prometheus also features technologies like closed-loop liquid cooling to help it operate efficiently.

Right now, in New Albany, Ohio, Meta is undertaking its most ambitious AI infrastructure project to date. Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster, is an advancement in our infrastructure that is training the next generation of foundational models that will bring new AI experiences to billions of people.

Two years ago, New Albany was a conventional data center site running web traffic. With advancements in hardware, networking and building design, we reworked this site to be home to training programs for frontier models. We’re building the supercluster in phases. The first phase has already been completed and was used to train our Muse foundational models, including the Muse Wonder models, our new frontier models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks.

Large training jobs require everything to work optimally to sustain their performance; an issue on a single host can slow down or stop the entire job, lowering its ‘goodput’. By focusing on improving our systems’ stability and reliability we were able to achieve more than 85% goodput for pre-training runs and more than 90% goodput for reinforcement learning (RL) runs of Muse Wonder. During these training runs, we were able to achieve an overall wall-clock mean time between interruptions (MTBI) of ~47k GPU hours. Since then, we have landed further changes across our fleet including firmware fixes to increase MTBI to more than 54K GPU hours, and we are constantly improving it.

Now, we’re continuing to scale Prometheus with our next frontier models from Meta Superintelligence Labs in mind.

The Prometheus supercluster is housed in Meta’s New Albany, Ohio, data center.

Today, Prometheus comprises an array of hundreds of thousands of GPUs across multiple interconnected buildings, including traditional and AI-optimized data center buildings and rapid deployment structures, all tightly interconnected by miles of fiber and functioning as a single machine.

This capacity allows us to pursue larger models and longer context windows than were previously practical. At full scale, Prometheus will comprise roughly 1 million distributed GPUs, all functioning in lockstep.

Prometheus currently deploys two NVIDIA GPU platforms, with a third (based on NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin NVL72) arriving soon. Each represents a generational leap in performance and efficiency, leveraging our NVL72 rack architecture where 72 GPUs act as a single accelerator within the same network fabric.

Our first platform, Catalina, leverages the NVIDIA GB200 NVL72. We deploy the Ariel variant, a two-rack configuration in which 36 GPUs per rack are interconnected via NVLink to form a unified 72-GPU domain. Catalina provides improvements in raw compute and memory capacity compared to Grand Teton H100. It leverages our Open Rack V3 (ORv3) high-power rack (HPR) structure, an open hardware design contributed to the Open Compute Project (OCP).

The Ariel variant of GB200 NVL72 pairs each NVIDIA Blackwell GPU with an NVIDIA Grace CPU and 2x NVIDIA ConnectX-7 400G NICs at a 1:1 CPU-to-GPU ratio, letting us deploy 800G of I/O per GPU earlier than the rest of the industry. We chose Ariel because the GB200 NVL72 scaled up nearly every other dimension relative to the NVIDIA H100: FLOPS, HBM bandwidth, scale-up bandwidth, and scale-up domain size, while scale-out bandwidth per GPU would have stayed at 400G. We expected that imbalance to cost performance, so we opted for a configuration that delivers 800G of scale-out per GPU. This also gave us more uniformity of spec as the region expanded over time and 800G scale-out became available.

Our second platform, Clemente, moves to the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 and improves on Catalina at both the GPU and the platform level. GB300 raises HBM capacity per GPU by 1.5x, from 192 GB to 288 GB, and dense FP4 throughput by a similar factor, while roughly doubling attention (softmax) acceleration. At the platform level, scale-out is no longer the constraint it was on the GB200 NVL72: NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNICs deliver 800G per GPU natively, so the capability we deployed early on Ariel becomes the baseline. That, together with a 2:1 GPU-to-CPU ratio, allows Clemente to pack the full 72-GPU domain into a single rack, streamlining our physical deployment. Clemente can be deployed with our modular Air-Assisted Liquid Cooling (AALC) or use Facility Liquid Cooling (FLC) in our newly designed data centers. Serviceability also improves substantially, with reduced cabling.

In traditional web services, the data center network transports requests and responses between services whose instances typically don’t require high bandwidth, high performance, and tight, lock-step coordination across many servers. Large-scale AI training requires all these, meaning the network that connects them is now an important part of AI workloads. To best address this, in addition to the standard data center network connecting servers, several years ago we added a second dedicated data network based on Ethernet, called the Back-End (BE) network, to enable direct GPU-to-GPU communication both within and across data center buildings.

Large pre-training jobs partition the training into data-parallel model replicas, creating a hierarchy in network usage: Latency-sensitive and bandwidth-sensitive operations concentrate within a replica, while traffic that is more tolerant of higher latency and less bandwidth is scheduled between replicas. Our network is designed to match this hierarchy, with low-latency, high-bandwidth fabrics within buildings and an aggregation network connecting the building fabrics.

We work closely with Meta Superintelligence Labs to ensure the parallelism design, traffic patterns, and communication algorithms and software are optimized to minimize exposure of any network communication. This keeps the GPUs as busy as possible and not waiting on the network.

The Meta team has employed these networking concepts in earlier building-scale, 24K GPU clusters and our region-scale, 100K+ GPU cluster over the last several years, and we took them to a new level of scale and distance in Prometheus.

At the building level, each Ethernet-based fabric interconnects up to 20,736 GPUs through a high-bandwidth, low-latency multi-layer topology. Our initial design used a Disaggregated Scheduled Fabric (DSF) to mitigate the network congestion caused by training collectives that typically have a small number of large, long-lived network flows that collide under traditional load-balancing techniques; it does this by utilizing sub-packet-level multipath routing and packet re-ordering in the fabric along with virtual output queues and credit-based end-to-end flow control.

As Ethernet NIC technology advanced, enabling packet re-ordering at the endpoint, we were able to update to a Non-Scheduled Fabric (NSF) utilizing shallow-buffer 51.2T Ethernet switches, such as Minipack3 with Dynamic Load Balancing and the NVIDIA Spectrum-4 switch ASIC-based Minipack3N with NVIDIA’s Adaptive Routing on ConnectX NICs. Both DSF and NSF are based on Meta’s FBOSS networking stack, giving us the control to rapidly iterate on and optimize the fabrics in Prometheus, and the visibility to operate these clusters at scale.

The Backend Aggregation (BAG) network is a multi-layer hub-and-spoke network that connects building-level fabrics across the Prometheus cluster, spanning 2 km to over 100 km. It is built with Arista 7800-series chassis running deep-buffered Broadcom Jericho3 silicon, delivering multiple Pbps of bandwidth per region pair.

Running pretraining over this network required a dedicated optimization effort with Meta Superintelligence Labs to ensure training was not slowed down, especially given speed-of-light constraints at these distances.

Pulling this all together, the complexity of the Prometheus network involves millions of miles of fiber strand, tens of thousands of switches, and millions of optics — from 2×400G FR4 LITE short-reach, low-cost pluggables inside the buildings to 800G-ZR coherent optics for links beyond ~10 km.

At Prometheus’ scale, every component needs to be monitored for reliability. A single fault anywhere can halt an entire training job and waste valuable compute resources.

Maintaining reliability at this level requires a co-engineering model with NVIDIA that goes beyond a traditional vendor dynamic. Teams are deeply embedded at our data centers, sharing real-time telemetry and running joint triage sessions to decompose every system halt by its root cause.

This attribution-driven accountability model ensures both sides are focused on targeted improvements. While Meta optimizes scheduling and infrastructure, NVIDIA addresses firmware, signal diagnostics, and memory handling. This transparency eliminates ambiguity and drives faster fixes across both organizations.

The transition from the H100 generation’s NVL8 architecture to NVL72 has fundamentally redefined our approach to infrastructure resilience. items.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
items.title_en: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites have long allowed bots to perform automated tasks, like capturing the content of web pages, but rules govern what they can access and how they behave. The web, after all, is designed primarily for people, even if we occasionally have to solve puzzles and captchas to prove we are not bots.

But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.

The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.

Facing degraded experiences and lost direct-ad revenue, major websites are aggressive blockades against consumer AI agents.

items.title_en:
It is becoming f*cking dangerous

A 21-year-old dev from China just ran 500 Claude Code agents in parallel and hooked them to a verification layer so none of them could bullshit him

He opens the live dashboard:
- 500 agents writing and checking at the same time
- Every output verified against the source in ~150 ms
- Three passes over 150 company profiles → zero errors left
- Everything dumped straight into an Obsidian vault

The trick is the split: one model does the work, a cheaper one decides if the claim is actually true. The loop doesn’t stop until everything checks out

An analyst team would bill weeks for this. He got it in one run

Same kind of Second Brain + swarm setup that keeps circulating. Bookmark the full breakdown

items.title: Town, which develops enterprise AI assistants, raised a $108M Series B at a $1B valuation, after announcing a $55M Series A in June (Dominic-Madori Davis/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Town, which develops enterprise AI assistants, raised a $108M Series B at a $1B valuation, after announcing a $55M Series A in June (Dominic-Madori Davis/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

Town, a two-year-old, San Francisco-based startup developing AI assistants, nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B funding round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. The company launched publicly just four months ago and said it reached millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue in a matter of weeks. It has raised at least $160 million to date, having previously announced a $55 million Series A round in June.

Town — founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze — is one of many AI assistants flooding the market right now. Town targets businesses, giving each employee an AI assistant called a Townie that helps with tasks by connecting to tools such as emails and calendars, as well as other core work systems. Employees’ Townies can talk to each other and share approved information; they can also now work with customers and others outside the company.

Alongside the funding, Town announced a shared workflow that automatically updates employees’ Townies with new business information rather than requiring each worker to update their own Townie. Andreessen Horowitz, Serena Ventures, and First Round Capital also participated in the round.

items.title: AI can write code, analyze data, and make decisions. But what happens when it needs to see a building that has changed,
items.title_en:
AI can write code, analyze data, and make decisions. But what happens when it needs to see a building that has changed, inspect a street, or get a fresh 3D view of a real place?

It needs someone on the ground.

That’s what caught my attention about @vangrid_io going live on Arc.

An AI agent can post a USDC bounty, get someone to visit the location and capture the area, then receive a 3D model built from that footage.

No need to send a robot across town. No need to rely on images that might be years old.

A person handles the capture, @vangrid_io turns it into usable spatial data, and the agent gets what it needs to keep working.

Robotics companies could get updated views of their surroundings. AI systems could access real-world information that simply isn't available online. And people with smartphones could earn money by helping these systems see places they cannot reach themselves.

AI still needs the physical world, even if it doesn't have a body.

Now there's a way to connect the two, with humans doing the work and onchain payments handling the reward.

This is one of the reasons I'm watching VanGrid.

People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again																				
				
																									
						

	
									
									
										

			Sarah Perez
	

									
									
								
					
					
						9:13 AM PDT · October 19, 2026											
																			
					
		
	





			
					
		
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
	





	
	
		
		
			
The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.

One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.”

Another, “cleanyourtv,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.

While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone. With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits.

Modern smart TVs ship with a technology called Automatic Content Recognition (ACR), which identifies what’s playing on the screen using screenshots, audio clips or other forms of digital fingerprinting.

If these “dumb TV” hacks become more popular among everyday consumers, they have the potential to disrupt the smart TV ad industry, which profits from selling viewing data to advertisers or using it to display personalized ads on their own interfaces.

As the creator of cleanyourtv, Gathin T., puts it, the idea to clean up the smart TV interface started one afternoon when he got tired of seeing the ads on his parents’ TV set.

Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon!It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher.Looks like an Apple TV now lol pic.twitter.com/E5Q4A1b0yI

“I had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi and build a simple home screen with just their apps on it. I put the prompt on GitHub, tweeted the before and after,s and a few thousand people did the same to their own TVs over the next two days. Xiaomi, TCL, Sony, Fire TV, LG, a projector or two,” the developer wrote on a website for donations, linked from the project’s homepage.

The solution doesn’t require gaining root access to the TV, nor does it make it impossible to return to the factory default state, if desired.

Meanwhile, the dumbtv solution has been tested end-to-end on a Fire TV Edition television set and Android/Google TV platforms on TVs from Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense, Xiaomi, and Shield. To use this hack, the developer, Muzammil Yasin Sabuwala, suggests pointing your preferred AI agent at the dumbtv repository on GitHub.

Sabuwala said he was motivated to work on dumbtv because he was tired of the ads and not being able to delve directly into the content he wanted to watch. His solution was coded using a combination of Deepseek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, he told TechCrunch, and he plans to maintain the GitHub, adding support for more models over time.

introducing dumbtv– no spying– no ads from tv– fully customisableto setup just point your agent to this repo – https://t.co/prQLD17Wa4 https://t.co/z41SWJZVXt pic.twitter.com/c6R8EhljiA

Fair warning: all these solutions are works in progress, and various users are now testing them across different TV platforms and suggesting updates and fixes.

However, individuals don’t need to borrow someone else’s work from GitHub to get the job done.

In one newly viral X post, Ryan Doyle explains that he simply sent Claude Code the listing for his TV and asked “Can you hack this?” The agent then talked him through the process, allowing him to remove the ads and bloatware from the TV set, speed up the lagging user interface, and customize his screensaver, he claims.

Doyle then goes on to demonstrate in a video how fast and responsive the new interface is after the AI made the requested changes.

This is how fast the TV moves now that Claude deleted all the BS laggy bloatware it comes with https://t.co/nUCEjqPwAO pic.twitter.com/g07CEgC1GJ

Seeing posts about people “vibe-coding their TVs,” inspired one X user, Mihir Gupta, to try it himself.

“One afternoon with Claude Code: 25 bloat apps disabled, the 192 MB stock launcher replaced with a custom 83 MB one, plus rotating wallpapers,” he wrote.

The end result of these hacks may be mixed, however. Some people have found that Claude wouldn’t respond to their simple suggestions to “hack my TV,” necessitating more complex prompts. Others warned that AI agents could make mistakes, possibly disabling important packages or breaking things in the process. One person even said they bricked their Android TV using Claude, and another got stuck halfway through hacking their Fire TV.

For those wary of using AI to fully hack their TVs, there are existing solutions for customizing Android-based smart TVs, such as home screen replacement apps ATV Launcher, Projectivity Launcher, and FLauncher.

items.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.title_en: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
“I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration.

Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.

After a summer filled with revelations that swarms of agents built by top firms like OpenAI and Anthropic have been breaking their containment and causing havoc on the public internet—often while those companies weren’t aware of what their agents were up to—the AI industry is desperate to get a better handle on the technology it has built.

items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Kling AI has released version 4.0 of its video generator with support for clips up to 30 seconds, ten keyframe images as input, and prompt comprehension expanded to 8,000 tokens. In comparisons with Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5, Kling 4.0 holds its own but doesn't pull ahead, which could be an early sign that the breakneck pace of progress in AI video models is starting to level off.

ai_analysis.briefing_en: Kling AI introduced version 4.0 of its video generation model, adding stereo audio, multilingual lip sync, and support for up to 30-second generations across ten keyframe inputs alongside a lightweight Flash variant. While holding strong against competing models, early signs suggest generative video improvements are entering a plateau.

elements_zh.what: 发布4.0大版本，扩容音频对齐与长视频功能并推轻量型号
elements_zh.why: 巩固视频赛道先发优势，在商业化变现与推理成本之间寻求平衡

elements_en.where: Generative video and multimodal tools sector
elements_en.what: Launched version 4.0 with stereo audio, lip syncing, and 30-second clips alongside a Flash model
elements_en.why: Defend lead while optimizing inference efficiency and commercial production pipeline

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI视频从一开始的‘满地六指怪物’狂奔到现在的超逼真运镜，只用了一年多。如今对口型和长时长都补齐了，但各家画质终于不再有神仙打架的震撼，说明哪怕是烧钱最猛的视频生成，也逃不过收益递减的物理铁律。
ai_analysis.insight_en: AI video sprinted from horrifying six-fingered abominations to photorealistic cinema in barely eighteen months. Now that everyone supports lip sync and long clips, the jaw-dropping leaps are drying up—proving even the flashiest generative sector eventually slams into diminishing marginal returns.

items.title:
THIS IS STUPIDLY F*CKING GOLD

7 raw inputs. 7 compilers. 50 of 50 sources fed into one linked wiki. This Opus 5.5 board
items.title_en:
THIS IS STUPIDLY F*CKING GOLD

7 raw inputs. 7 compilers. 50 of 50 sources fed into one linked wiki. This Opus 5.5 board has a notes trick almost nobody uses.

The idea: stop storing notes in 7 separate piles. Every pile goes through its own compiler and comes out as linked knowledge. The counter starts at 9 of 50, and the owl only finishes when it hits 50.

No forgotten Claude Code sessions, no unread raw notes, and you can see which source feeds which part of the wiki.

The whole pipeline is one line:
sources → compiler → owl

here's the split:
→ code, docs and SQL go into graphify, a queryable knowledge graph
→ a whole project goes into Understand-Anything, a graph you learn from your codebase
→ sources you read once go into claude-obsidian, grounded answers
→ Claude Code sessions go into obsidian-second-brain, plain markdown memory
→ your chats go into claude-code-memory-setup, vault plus code graphs
→ raw notes go into second-brain, maintained by the LLM
→ collected files go into llm-wikid, cross-linked wiki pages

You only look at three moments:
→ 9 of 50 fed: the owl is a few loose blocks
→ 36 of 50: the shape is there, still full of holes
→ 50 of 50: compiled wiki, linked

↳ the footer says it straight: the compiler is not the brain, the brain is what you feed it
